Title: From collecting coins for rice and petrol to a Mitsubishi XForce
Article:
KUALA LANGAT: Syahidatul Azimah Azmi, who once collected coins with her husband to buy rice and petrol, was moved to tears when he surprised her with a Mitsubishi XForce.
According to Harian Metro, Syahidatul, 34, said the gift from her husband, Abubakar Sanusi, 30, reminded her of how far they had come since tying the knot in September 2016, and of the challenges they had overcome together.
She said she had never expected to receive the Mitsubishi XForce, as their Proton Persona, which they had used since 2012, before their marriage, had become increasingly prone to breakdowns, making daily travel difficult.
"I only asked my husband for a Perodua Axia, as long as I had a vehicle that was easy to use to get around," she said.
The couple met at Madrasah Syeikhul Ariffien in Melaka, where Syahidatul worked and Abubakar was a student.
They decided to marry after three months of getting to know each other seriously.
Although both came from financially comfortable families, they chose to build a life of their own after marriage.
Syahidatul said their limited income in the early years meant they had to be careful with their spending, as Abubakar was training as a car mechanic on a monthly allowance of RM250 while she earned RM1,000.
"Our limited income meant we had to be frugal to meet all our commitments. There was a point when we had to collect coins to buy petrol and rice," she said.
Despite their struggles, the couple remained determined to improve their circumstances.
Abubakar now runs a car workshop in Bandar Saujana Putra, enabling them to enjoy a more stable life.
Syahidatul said the Mitsubishi XForce left her surprised and emotional, as it reminded her of their journey from struggling to afford basic necessities to enjoying a more comfortable life.
"When I think about it, we have come a long way, from trying to scrape together enough money to buy rice and petrol to where we are today.
"It's not just about the car. Looking back at our journey since the beginning of our marriage, we have been through so much together.
"Alhamdulillah, I am grateful for what we have today," she said.

Title: RoS confirms PN's deregistration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has confirmed that Perikatan Nasional's registration has been cancelled, saying the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
RoS said the decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after reviewing all documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
It said a notice dated Sept 22 had been issued to PN under subsection 13(2) of the Act, allowing the coalition to provide explanations and representations on the matters raised.
"After reviewing all documents and explanations submitted, the Registrar of Societies found that the reasons given failed to refute the grounds for cancellation of registration stated in the notice.
"They also did not provide sufficient justification to maintain the organisation's registration," it said.

Title: Malaysia has made no commitment to provide financing support to AirAsia, ministry says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial assistance to budget airline operator AirAsia, the finance ministry said, though it acknowledged concerns over the carrier's financial health following a jump in jet fuel prices.
Reuters reported this month, citing sources, that AirAsia was in talks with the government over potential support. The airline's co-founder Tony Fernandes said the talks focused on aviation-related costs such as airport charges and fuel, not financial assistance.
In a written parliamentary reply on Monday, the finance ministry said it was monitoring developments in Malaysia's aviation sector, including recent quarterly losses reported by AirAsia that were attributed to rising fuel costs stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran.
The government was regularly engaging with aviation players and seeking views from industry and technical experts, as was the case for other economic sectors affected by the Middle East crisis, it said.
Any request for support from companies in any sector "will be considered based on the interests of the country and the people, the fiscal sustainability of the government and the protection of public funds, in accordance with applicable laws and procedures," the ministry said.
"To date, the government has not made any agreement or commitment to provide financing support to AirAsia, whether in the form of guarantees, loans or public fund injections," it said.
The ministry said AirAsia was a significant player in the aviation sector, accounting for around 41 per cent of the 104.5 million passenger movements recorded at airports operated by Malaysia Airports Holdings in 2025 and almost 60 per cent of domestic passenger movements.
The carrier also played a significant role in maintaining air connectivity in Malaysia's Sabah and Sarawak states on Borneo Island, it said.

Title: Malaysia CPO tax waivers could lift plantation stocks as inventory hits record high
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's plantation sector could receive a timely boost if the government waives crude palm oil (CPO) export tax to help clear swelling inventories, restore export competitiveness and claw back market share from Indonesia.
According to a wires report, the government is considering the proposal amid an oversupply situation, with the Plantation and Commodities Ministry expected to discuss the matter with industry players today.
Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) analyst Chong Hoe Leong believes the proposed waiver could benefit upstream plantation companies by making Malaysian palm oil more competitive in international markets, particularly as Indonesia's exports gain ground while Malaysia grapples with mounting inventories.
"We believe the proposal would be well received and likely will take effect soon. The waiver of CPO export tax will help Malaysia regain market share from Indonesia," he said in a note.
Malaysia's CPO inventory reached a record 3.5 million tonnes last month, reflecting the pressure on exporters from the price gap between Malaysian and Indonesian palm oil.
At the current 10 per cent CPO export tax rate in Malaysia, compared with Indonesia's combined export duty and levy of US$273 per tonne (RM1,113 per tonne), Indonesian CPO has been trading at a discount of RM700 to RM900 per tonne against Malaysian prices.
"This wide discount has put Malaysia's CPO exporters at a disadvantage, resulting in a significant loss of market share to our counterparts and a record inventory level of 3.5 million tonnes last month.
"This is evident as Indonesian palm oil exports have grown, in contrast to Malaysia's lacklustre performance," Chong said.
The price differential has put Malaysian exporters at a disadvantage, contributing to weaker export performance and allowing Indonesia to capture a larger share of the global market.
A waiver could narrow the competitiveness gap and provide relief to local exporters, particularly following India's reduction of its CPO import tax to five per cent from 10 per cent.
Malaysia previously waived CPO export tax for six months in 2020.
"We suggest the CPO tax waiver should be in place until the inventory level falls below 2.0 million tonnes."
However, the benefits would not be evenly distributed across the sector.
Chnong said upstream plantation companies stand to gain from stronger demand and potentially improved selling prices, while downstream players could face margin pressure if cheaper raw materials become less readily available.
The potential policy shift comes as plantation companies prepare to report their third-quarter 2026 results, with Chong anticipating stronger earnings on the back of higher fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production, lower production costs and firmer CPO prices.
He said that all plantation companies under coverage recorded production growth, led by Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, whose output rose 30 per cent year-on-year, followed by Sarawak Plantation Bhd at 23.2 per cent and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd at 16.4 per cent.
Average CPO prices also strengthened to RM4,552 per tonne in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RM4,275 per tonne a year earlier, providing further support for earnings.
Against this backdrop, Chong maintains an "Overweight" call on the plantation sector, with Sarawak Plantation and Ta Ann emerging as preferred picks for their attractive dividend yields and above-industry-average FFB production growth.
The combination of potentially stronger export competitiveness, improving production and attractive dividend yields could support the sector's performance in the second half of 2026, although the actual impact will depend on whether the government proceeds with the proposed tax waiver and how quickly inventories normalise.

Title: In search for Amelia Earhart's plane, tantalising clue turns out to be tree debris
Article:
LOS ANGELES: US-based explorers who travelled to a tiny South Pacific island seeking to conclusively solve the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart have determined that an object they suspected was wreckage from her plane was a cluster of washed-up trees.
The mission leaders made the announcement on Monday. The team set out this month from Los Angeles for the archipelago nation of Kiribati on a US$900,000 expedition backed by private donors and Indiana's Purdue University, which has long been associated with Earhart and her legacy.
The objective was to determine whether an elongated, multi-pronged object detected in 2020 satellite imagery in the island's lagoon was a remnant of Earhart's long-missing twin-engine Lockheed Electra 10-E aeroplane.
Such a finding would have decisively supported the hypothesis held by some scholars that Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, crash-landed on or near the coral-ringed atoll and died as castaways there, hundreds of miles from their intended refuelling stop.
'Adventure is worthwhile'
"Unfortunately, we weren't able to find that smoking gun," Purdue general counsel and team member Steve Schultz said in a video message recorded on the island of Nikumaroro, part of the Phoenix Islands in Kiribati.
Quoting Earhart, he added: "You know, Amelia herself said, 'Adventure is worthwhile in itself.'"
After a week on the island, the team ultimately concluded that the "visual anomaly" detected by satellite "was likely a collection of large trees" wedged in the lagoon's sand, the expedition said in a statement.
Much of the debris had fragmented and washed away since it was first spotted, leaving a smaller Y-shaped segment whose reflective surface — suggestive of metal — turned out to come from "its carbonate veneer", the team said.
Two previous attempts to locate the aircraft's wreckage in the ocean around Nikumaroro also proved fruitless, while a plane-shaped sonar image captured elsewhere on the sea floor turned out to be a pile of rocks.
Earhart and Noonan were last seen taking off in the Electra on July 2, 1937, from Papua New Guinea, during Earhart's multi-stage attempt to become the first woman to pilot an aeroplane around the world and the first aviator to circumnavigate the equator.
Radio contact with the flight was lost the next day after Earhart, 39, reported that "gas is running low", followed by her final known transmission giving her navigational line of position.
Castaway hypothesis 'remains very strong'
The disappearance prompted one of the largest air-sea searches ever undertaken and remains one of the great unsolved mysteries of the 20th century and aviation history.
The expedition's leader, Richard Pettigrew, head of the Archaeological Legacy Institute in Eugene, Oregon, said evidence supporting the "castaway hypothesis" — that Earhart and Noonan died while marooned on Nikumaroro — "remains very strong".
He cited evidence collected over more than 30 years by veteran Earhart explorer Ric Gillespie, co-founder of The International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery and author of the 2024 book One More Good Flight: The Amelia Earhart Tragedy.
Gillespie's case includes multiple radio distress calls picked up in the days immediately after Earhart vanished, with bearings converging on Nikumaroro, and a 2018 forensic analysis of human bones recovered on the island in 1940 that found they belonged to a woman of Earhart's build and stature.
Gillespie's investigation also encompassed artefacts found on the island, including a woman's shoe, a compact case, a freckle cream jar and a medicine vial, all dating to the 1930s, as well as remnants of a jackknife similar to one Earhart carried on the plane.
Another piece of evidence is a photograph taken of the island's shoreline months after Earhart vanished, showing an object that appears to be the Electra's landing gear.
The Purdue expedition said this month that it had uncovered several other artefacts, including a 30-inch-long steel tube found in the lagoon, that could yield further evidence when studied.
According to Gillespie, the plane has been lost to history, eventually swept by tides off the coral flat where it had landed and carried into the sea, where it sank and broke apart in the surf.
The official US government view of Earhart's fate has long been that her plane ran out of fuel and crashed at sea near its intended refuelling destination of Howland Island, another small island about 640km northwest of Nikumaroro.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: France's unrest lays bare 'slow agony' of Macron's twilight months
Article:
FRANCE'S worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron's final months in office deeper into turmoil, exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order.
The rioting that swept across France on Saturday, leaving a trail of looted shops, torched buildings and defaced public institutions, presents Macron with perhaps the most explosive challenge of his twilight presidency: a country demanding more from a state that can no longer afford to give much.
Macron came to power almost a decade ago promising to upend France's sclerotic political class, turbocharge economic reforms and restore authority through a more assertive presidency.
Instead, with just six months left in office, he finds himself effectively a lame-duck head of state presiding over a country mired in political paralysis, facing acute financial pressures and grappling with unrest that has exposed the limits of state authority.
Unlike during the Yellow Vest uprising of 2018-2019, when Macron sought to defuse public anger with billions of euros in concessions, France's strained public finances and fractured parliament leave him with precious few levers to pull.
Even former allies are now openly scathing, tracing the country's current impasse to Macron's decision to call a snap parliamentary election in 2024 that weakened his authority.
"The end of this term is a slow agony," said Loïc Kervran, a former lawmaker from Macron's camp, on X.
"The president paralysed the country with his absurd decision to dissolve parliament in 2024. Arguably the worst decision in the history of the Fifth Republic."
The turmoil may benefit far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, who is already the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race and stands to gain from both the anger over declining living standards and the fears over law and order unleashed by the weekend's violence.
"Le Pen no longer needs to spend any money to campaign," Jean-Baptiste Moreau, another former Macron lawmaker, told Reuters. "It's not just a clear path ahead of her — it's a six-lane highway."
Le Pen delivered her own message to the nation in a video statement on Sunday, portraying Macron's administration as a crumbling power and casting herself as the figure capable of restoring order.
[[nid:1559442]]
When Macron later addressed the country, he offered little concrete action, stopping short of declaring a state of emergency.
Opponents and one-time allies alike were underwhelmed. His former prime minister, Edouard Philippe, now preparing his own presidential run, was unsparing in his criticism.
"Mr President, I listened to you last night," he wrote on X. "I would have preferred, like millions of French people, decisions and initiatives to restore order."
But even Philippe is struggling to shake off his past association with Macron, and most recent polls show far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon edging ahead of him in the race to qualify for the second-round runoff vote.
That outcome would all but guarantee a Le Pen victory, according to opinion polls.
Investors also took fright. Market analysts say the violence adds another layer of political risk at a time when France is already under scrutiny over its swelling debt burden and struggle to reduce one of the euro zone's largest budget deficits.
The president now finds himself trapped between bond markets demanding spending restraint and protesters demanding the opposite.
Despite calls from opponents to remain in France, Macron arrived in Kuwait on Monday on a Gulf tour he says will help secure fuel supplies and ease some of the economic pressures that have helped swell the ranks of the protesters.
The trip carries risks, reinforcing perceptions of a president disconnected from the public mood.
Images of Macron attending a Celine Dion concert with his wife Brigitte on Friday evening, hours before the unrest erupted, prompted ridicule on social media and became an easy symbol for critics seeking to portray him as detached from events.
Moreau, who spoke to Macron on Sunday, said he urged him to prepare an orderly early departure to break the current political deadlock and avoid another six months of drift.
"He doesn't want to give up, that's not his character. But that's what he should do for the country," he said.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Dollar, euro drift as markets seek direction, yen slips
Article:
SINGAPORE: The US dollar traded in a narrow range in early Asian trading on Tuesday as a tentative recovery in investor confidence supported higher-yielding currencies, while rising political risks in Europe continued to unsettle markets.
The euro was steady at US$1.1216, while the British pound rose 0.1 per cent to US$1.3308. The Australian dollar gained 0.1 per cent to US$0.6986, while the New Zealand dollar edged up 0.1 per cent to US$0.5668.
Against the yen, the US dollar was flat at 158.56 yen ahead of an auction of 20-year Japanese government bonds.
"FX markets reflected the improvement in risk appetite, with higher-carry currencies finding buyers," Pepperstone Group head of research Chris Weston said.
"Europe was less convincing," Weston said. "French sovereign risk is clearly being priced into European equities, but the euro's resilience suggests traders aren't yet treating it as a systemic European problem."
French authorities imposed curfews in several cities on Monday after nationwide anti-government protests plunged President Emmanuel Macron's final months in office into turmoil.
In Italy, the government said it would deploy 500 troops following two days of unrest.
"The spread of French government bonds over Germany has come under renewed widening pressure against the backdrop of violent protests grabbing the headlines," ING analysts said in a client note.
"Tuesday will likely see more headlines around the 2027 budget, as (the French) Parliament is slated for a first formal vote on the revenue section of the finance bill."
The spread between French and German 10-year government bonds widened 9.9 basis points on Monday to 147.3 basis points. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond was flat at 5.131 per cent.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback against six major currencies, ended a two-day losing streak on Monday, rising 0.2 per cent to 101.98.
Against the Chinese yuan, the US dollar was flat at 6.6811 yuan in offshore trading after the People's Bank of China kept interest rates unchanged, in line with market expectations.
Bitcoin was flat at US$81,906.58, while ether edged up 0.3 per cent to US$2,405.99.

Title: Perak smallholders suffer losses as elephants ravage oil palm plots
Article:
SUNGAI SIPUT: Eighteen oil palm smallholders in Rancangan Tanah Belia Khas (RTBK) Kampung Perlop 1 here are facing mounting distress after a herd of wild elephants destroyed their crops spanning about 81 hectares since early September.
One of the affected smallholders, Mastura Yusuf, 65, said her 12.1-ha plot suffered severe damage, with over 300 oil palm trees destroyed, particularly three-year-old saplings.
Mastura, who has been farming the land since 2002, said it was the worst destruction she had experienced from continuous elephant attacks.
She said the wild elephants also damaged farm infrastructure, including water storage containers and concrete water tanks.
She added that the intrusions not only threatened the main source of income for her and fellow villagers, but also ruined repeated replanting efforts.
She said the elephant intrusions had become increasingly frequent this year, particularly in September and October, forcing her to bear replanting costs for four separate cycles.
"If it costs RM35 just to plant a single tree, you can imagine how much loss I have suffered, not including other costs such as worker wages, fertiliser, and pesticides.
"We noticed the elephant attacks starting last year, but they have become more frequent recently, especially at night," she said when met at the plantation yesterday.
Another smallholder, Muhammad Azlan Adnan, 42, said two hectares of his six-hectare oil palm plot suffered extensive damage, particularly to the shoots and leaves.
"For smaller trees, the impact is worse because once pulled by an elephant, the tree dies instantly. Based on tracks, footprint sizes, and dung left behind, there are probably two or three elephants that entered my farm," he said.
Meanwhile, Mohd Faiz Ahmad, 40, said 120 out of 550 oil palm trees on his land were trampled and uprooted, resulting in losses between RM16,000 and RM17,000 in land preparation, pesticides, fertiliser, and replanting costs.
He said the severe disruption left most smallholders drained of capital and demoralised from continuing maintenance work for upcoming crops.
"Therefore, we appeal for intervention and financial assistance from relevant government agencies to ease our financial burden," he said.

Title: Haze: Batu Muda, Johan Setia among 29 areas with unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded the highest unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 172 as of 8.30am today, followed by Johan Setia in Selangor at 171, according to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
Of the 29 areas on the unhealthy list, Petaling Jaya and Shah Alam in Selangor recorded readings of 166 and 165 respectively, while Nilai in Negri Sembilan registered 165 and Port Dickson 145.
Cheras recorded 164, followed by Bukit Rambai in Melaka (163), Putrajaya and Klang in Selangor (both 162), Seremban in Negri Sembilan (159) and Banting in Selangor (158).
In Johor, Larkin recorded 157, followed by Pasir Gudang (156), Kota Tinggi (154), Kluang and Pengerang (both 151), Tangkak (131) and Batu Pahat (130).
Alor Gajah in Melaka recorded 155, while Bandaraya Melaka registered 152. In Perak, Tasek Ipoh recorded 155, followed by Pegoh Ipoh at 152.
In the east coast, Paka in Terengganu recorded 155, followed by Rompin in Pahang (153), Balok Baru in Kuantan (152), Jerantut (137), Indera Mahkota in Kuantan (125) and Temerloh (103).
Meanwhile, 32 areas recorded moderate API readings.
In the east coast, Kemaman in Terengganu recorded 99, followed by Kuala Terengganu (81) and Besut (63). Kota Baru in Kelantan registered 65, while Tanah Merah recorded 63.
In Kedah, Sungai Petani recorded 89, followed by Kulim Hi-Tech (84) and Alor Star (60).
In Penang, Seberang Jaya recorded 88, followed by Seberang Perai (86), Minden (83) and Balik Pulau (53). Kangar in Perlis recorded 56.
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded 98, followed by Tanjung Malim (97) and Taiping (96).
In Johor, Segamat recorded 88, while Kuala Selangor in Selangor registered 100.
In Sabah, Tawau recorded 79, followed by Keningau (57) and Sandakan (54).
In Sarawak, Sri Aman recorded 92, followed by Samarahan and Serian (both 87), Kuching (84), Sibu (76), Sarikei (73), Mukah (72), Kapit (70), Samalaju and Bintulu (both 58) and Miri (52).
Seven areas recorded good API readings.
Kota Kinabalu and Politeknik Kota Kinabalu in Sabah both recorded 49, followed by Langkawi in Kedah (46), Labuan (45), Limbang in Sarawak (35), ILP Miri in Sarawak (32) and Kimanis in Sabah (30).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.

Title: National Australia Bank to cut 2,500 jobs in cost overhaul as credit growth slows
Article:
BENGALURU: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) will cut up to 2,500 jobs, or about six per cent of its workforce, over the next year to simplify operations and reduce costs amid pressure on Australia's credit growth.
The bank, Australia's biggest business lender and third-largest home lender, said up to 1,500 positions would be cut by the end of 2026.
The largest cuts will target corporate roles rather than customer-facing bankers, while the bank also plans to materially reduce its reliance on consultants and contractors.
"Our ambition and strategy remain unchanged. We will improve productivity, risk outcomes and execution to be a simpler and more efficient bank," chief executive Andrew Irvine said in a statement.
NAB shares fell nearly 2.5 per cent on Tuesday, recording the biggest decline among Australia's four major retail banks. The S&P/ASX 200 index was down 0.9 per cent.
NAB said it would begin consultations with the Finance Sector Union, whose national assistant secretary Nicole McPherson said the job cuts would not help simplify the organisation.
"To take a wrecking ball to 6% of one of Australia's largest workforces this close to Christmas is disgraceful and shows that NAB's leadership is completely detached from the lived experience of their workers," she said.
The restructuring will incur a pre-tax charge of about A$300 million (US$209 million) in 2027, covering redundancy, redeployment and organisational redesign costs.
This compares with pre-tax charges of about A$80 million in each of 2025 and 2026, NAB said.
The job cuts come as Australia's banks face mounting pressure from weaker housing activity, intensifying competition and higher operating costs, which are weighing on earnings.
In August, NAB warned that housing credit growth would slow sharply in 2027 following the federal government's property tax reforms, which the bank said had dampened demand from homebuyers and investors.
At the time, Irvine said geopolitical uncertainty, higher domestic interest rates and tax changes were creating challenges for customers.
NAB employed 41,880 people globally as at Sept 30, 2025, according to its latest annual report.
The move follows a similar restructuring drive by rival ANZ, which last year announced plans to cut about 3,500 jobs by September 2026 under chief executive Nuno Matos as part of a programme to simplify operations, reduce duplication and lower costs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police, activists move cats to safety after viral video sparks outrage
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: Police and animal welfare activists have removed several cats from the home of a suspect arrested after a video showing him committing an indecent act involving a cat went viral.
District police chief Superintendent Saari Yaacob said the animals were relocated to ensure their safety following the 49-year-old suspect's arrest at 10am yesterday.
The cat involved in the incident was handed over to the Veterinary Services Department for further examination.
Saari said police are investigating the suspect's mental health status following claims that he has psychological issues.
"We have yet to receive medical confirmation or documentation regarding his condition.
"To protect the remaining cats from harm, we have moved them to a care centre," he said when met in Selinsing last night.
The suspect was detained after a 56-second video showing the
alleged act
triggered public outrage online.
Saari warned the public against sharing the video, noting that offenders face action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which carries a maximum fine of RM500,000, up to two years' imprisonment, or both.
Meanwhile, animal welfare activist Nur Izyan Syahida Rosli said she had taken two cats from the suspect's home to be cared for under the Kelab Pencinta Haiwan Pewaris Kelantan.
She added that the group is prepared to adopt the cat involved in the incident once police complete their investigation.
"We are ready to take in the cat if permitted by the authorities after investigations conclude," she said.

Title: Oil eases as markets assess Russian energy waiver, Middle East supply risks
Article:
BENGALURU: Oil prices fell on Tuesday as markets weighed an executive order by US President Donald Trump waiving some sanctions and tariffs linked to Russian energy exports, while attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen kept concerns over Middle East supply disruptions in focus.
Brent crude futures fell 49 cents, or 0.45 per cent, to US$109.06 a barrel by 8.10am Malaysian time.
The US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude contract for November delivery, which expires on Tuesday, eased 0.33 per cent to US$103.32. The more actively traded December contract fell 46 cents, or 0.47 per cent, to US$98.08.
Brent rose to US$110.70 a barrel in the previous session, its highest since May 20.
An executive order issued by Trump on Friday night waived key US sanctions and tariffs related to Russia, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas. However, Trump said on Saturday that he had yet to make a final decision on the matter, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials wanted more time to evaluate the situation.
Russia's crude oil production rose by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day, but remained about 870,000 barrels per day below a year earlier, the International Energy Agency said last week.
"While the prospect of additional Russian diesel supply offers some theoretical relief, traders appear far more focused on the ongoing risk of further damage to energy infrastructure across the Gulf region," KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer said.
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they had carried out several attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, including an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha airport.
Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims, and Reuters could not independently verify them.
Meanwhile, 58 people were killed and more than 200 injured in a Houthi attack on a government security forces training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province on Monday.
The renewed attacks heightened concerns over regional stability and underscored the continuing risks to energy supplies from the region, keeping oil prices above US$100 a barrel.
In the US, crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last week, along with inventories of refined products, a preliminary Reuters poll showed on Monday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vote count begins in Alberta secession referendum, testing Canadian unity
Article:
EDMONTON: Vote counting was underway in Canada's province of Alberta on Monday, as the oil-rich province decided whether to hold a binding independence referendum, testing national unity amid a crisis in relations with the United States.
Prime Minister Mark Carney has in recent days argued that Alberta's vote is being held "at the worst possible time", urging Canadians to rally together to confront US President Donald Trump's trade war and annexation threats.
Polls indicated that less than a quarter of people in the western province wanted independence, but separatist leader Mitch Sylvestre told AFP on Monday that he remained optimistic.
"We're hoping to win," said Sylvestre, who heads the Alberta Prosperity Project, at a restaurant in the provincial capital, Edmonton, where his side was watching the returns.
Most polling stations were due to close at 8pm (0200 GMT Tuesday), but more than 100 would close later because of delayed openings, Alberta's elections authority said.
Elections Alberta said 1.4 million of the 3.1 million eligible voters had cast advance ballots. Those ballots were being counted from 5pm.
Results might not be available until the early hours of Tuesday, Elections Alberta said.
David Gallagher, who voted earlier on a chilly Edmonton morning, told AFP that an independent Alberta was a "silly idea".
"I want to stamp it down and stop it," the 58-year-old said.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, a conservative, has said she will vote against independence but called the referendum to settle an issue that has divided the province.
If a majority votes to separate, she has pledged to move forward with a binding referendum.
If the federalists win, Smith said the secession question should be considered closed.
Foreign influence?
Alberta has the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves, and much of the separatist momentum has been driven by anger over the management of the oil industry.
Smith has blamed Carney's predecessor, Justin Trudeau, for igniting the separatist movement, accusing him of trying to crush oil production to advance his pro-climate agenda.
Alberta's independence push has also drawn sustained interest from Trump allies.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Alberta a "natural partner" for the United States. Elon Musk, the world's richest person and a top Trump supporter, posted on X this month that Alberta "should separate".
Separatist leaders have also held meetings at the US State Department and with Republican political operatives.
'Huge uncertainty'
Carney, who grew up in Alberta, has worked to improve relations between the province and Ottawa since taking office last year.
He has partnered with Smith to advance a new pipeline to export more Alberta bitumen overseas, a project considered a non-starter during Trudeau's tenure.
But he has also warned Albertans that even a non-binding vote on independence would be a "dangerous bluff", drawing on his experience during Brexit, when he was governor of the Bank of England.
He said the "huge uncertainty" that followed the Brexit vote hurt the British economy, cautioning Alberta against unintended economic consequences.
Sylvestre said Carney had "threatened" the province in the closing days of the campaign.
Carney's message was "voting against Canada is dangerous", Sylvestre said. "I think that's very, very unreasonable."
Haley Erdegard, a 44-year-old who voted in Edmonton, voiced discomfort with the idea advanced by some separatists that Alberta was forced to share too much of its oil revenue with the rest of Canada.
"The whole point of privilege is that if you have more than somebody else, you're supposed to share," she told AFP.
"I think we probably need to put some more work towards cooperation before making rash decisions about trying to start our own country."

Title: Woman killed as trailer runs red light, rams car in Machang
Article:
MACHANG: A 26-year-old woman was killed when her car was rammed by a trailer that ran a red light at Km4.7 of Jalan Machang-Tanah Merah, near the Wakaf Bata traffic light junction, here last night.
In the 10.30pm incident, the victim died at the scene from severe injuries.
District police chief Superintendent Azuhar Md Nor said initial investigations revealed that the Volvo trailer, driven by a 47-year-old man, was travelling from Tanah Merah towards Machang.
"The trailer is believed to have run a red light at the junction before crashing into the right side of the Perodua Axia, which was moving from Padang Kelupang towards Tanah Merah.
"The heavy impact caused the Perodua Axia driver to suffer severe injuries, and she was pronounced dead at the scene.
"The trailer driver was unhurt," he said in a statement today.
He added that the victim's body was sent to Sultan Ismail Petra Hospital in Kuala Krai for an autopsy.
"The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless and dangerous driving.
"The trailer driver was also arrested under Section 30 of the Poisons Act 1952 after police seized four transparent plastic packages containing a brownish liquid suspected to be ketum water," he said.
Those with information can contact Machang district police headquarters traffic investigating officer Inspector Khairulanwar Adam at 011-10085165 or visit the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher as inflation eases, OPR normalisation in focus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Tuesday despite a stronger greenback, supported by easing domestic inflation and expectations of a possible normalisation of the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR).
At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0780/0850 against the US dollar, compared with Monday's close of 4.0805/0845.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) reported that inflation eased to 1.8 per cent in September 2026, from 1.9 per cent in August.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expected the ringgit to trade within a range of RM4.07 to RM4.08 against the US dollar today.
He said investors were also monitoring geopolitical risks in West Asia after Iran's navy reported an attack by the US military on the Konarak naval base.
"We are entering the blackout period, during which US Federal Reserve officials will not be commenting publicly ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting," he told Bernama.
The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the greenback against a basket of major currencies, rose 0.15 per cent to 101.989 points, he added.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5724/5770 from 2.5790/5817 at Monday's close, and rose against the British pound to 5.4274/4367 from 5.4369/4422.
However, it edged lower against the euro to 4.5731/5809 from 4.5726/5771 previously.
The ringgit also strengthened against most of its ASEAN peers.
It edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 225.9/226.4 from 226.0/226.4 on Monday, and against the Philippine peso to 6.46/6.48 from 6.47/6.48.
The local currency also rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.1862/1919 from 3.1886/1920 at the previous close, and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1373/1661 from 12.1451/1613.

Title: Haze may ease by month-end as monsoon rains arrive - Academic
Article:
ARAU: The haze affecting Malaysia is expected to gradually improve by the end of this month as the country enters the monsoon transition phase, which could bring more rain and changes in wind direction and speed.
Universiti Malaysia Perlis (Unimap) Faculty of Civil Engineering and Technology associate professor Dr Norazian Mohamed Noor said these factors could help reduce atmospheric pollutant concentrations and limit the cross-border movement of smoke from Indonesia.
She said the Malaysian Meteorological Department's (MetMalaysia) long-range weather outlook for October to March 2027 indicated that most parts of the country were expected to receive rainfall close to their climatological averages from this month until December.
Selangor, for example, was forecast to receive between 220mm and 330mm of rain this month, and between 250mm and 380mm in November.
Kuala Lumpur, meanwhile, was expected to receive between 240mm and 360mm of rain in October, rising to between 300mm and 450mm in November.
"These conditions offer a positive indication that increased rainfall could help improve air quality in Malaysia. However, the recovery may not occur simultaneously across all areas.
"Haze conditions are influenced not only by rainfall in Malaysia but also by fire activity, rainfall distribution in pollution-source areas and wind direction.
"Rainfall in our country alone is insufficient to ensure an end to transboundary haze if fires remain active at their source in Indonesia," she said recently.
Norazian said an analysis by Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), dated Oct 13, indicated that parts of southern Sumatra, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan were still expected to receive low rainfall of less than 50mm over certain 10-day periods this month.
She said the conditions could increase the risk of forest and peatland fires, particularly in areas experiencing prolonged dry spells.
"However, the BMKG forecast also indicated increased rainfall in several parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan in November and December, with some areas potentially receiving more than 300mm of rain a month.
"Should the rainfall be continuous and cover fire-affected areas, it could help reduce fire activity and smoke emissions," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Threatened with arrest, housewife loses RM472,000 to scammers
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A 46-year-old housewife here lost RM472,000 after falling victim to a phone scam syndicate.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim lodged a police report at 10.30am yesterday.
On Aug 5, the woman received a call from an individual identifying himself as "Mohd Farhan Jamil", claiming to be from the Communications Ministry.
The caller informed her that she was involved in spreading unauthorised information regarding investment shares, government assistance, and job opportunities.
"The individual then claimed her call was being transferred to the Kajang police headquarters, where she spoke to 'Sergeant Andi'.
"The suspect impersonating Sergeant Andi instructed the victim to read out her identity card number. After performing a 'check', he claimed she was involved in money laundering activities," Azli said.
The suspect also told her that an arrest warrant had been issued in her name.
The call was subsequently transferred to a deputy public prosecutor named Zaleha. To resolve the matter, Zaleha instructed the victim to transfer funds, promising the money would be returned upon completion of the investigation.
Fearing arrest, the victim made 21 transactions into three separate bank accounts between Aug 18 and Sept 19, amounting to RM472,000.
"After completing the payments, she was asked to transfer an additional RM80,000, but she refused. Realising she had been cheated, she lodged a police report," Azli added.
The funds involved were the victim's personal savings.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Corporate mafia', abuse of power issues to take centre stage in Dewan Rakyat today
