Title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after 43 years [WATCH]
Article:
NEW YORK: Veteran journalist Christiane Amanpour said on Monday that she was leaving her role at CNN after a 43-year career as one of the US broadcaster's most prominent international correspondents.
"After thinking carefully for several months and experiencing a few sleepless nights, as you can imagine, I've decided to separate from CNN," Amanpour, 68, said in a statement.
Her announcement came weeks after media corporation Paramount Skydance formally took over Warner Bros. Discovery, the parent company of CNN.
The merger has raised concerns over CNN's independence, as the merged company's owners, the Ellison family, are close allies of US President Donald Trump — a fierce critic of the television network.
Amanpour did not reference the deal but emphasised her commitment to being "fiercely independent".
"That's especially important today as we face unprecedented pressures from all sides, political, financial, and also from the rising dangers in the field," she said.
British-born Amanpour first became known to CNN's international audience for her coverage of the 1991 Gulf War, which followed Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
She has interviewed many of the world's leaders and newsmakers over the past decades and reported from hotspots such as Iraq, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Somalia, Rwanda and the Balkans.
Amanpour said her daily news show on CNN would be scaled back to once a week until next June, while her PBS programme would also end.
She added that she "looks forward to interesting new projects down the line, and will always be rooting for CNN and maintaining its history of independent journalism. Remember: always be truthful, not neutral."
In a memo carried by US media, CNN chief executive Mark Thompson praised Amanpour "for 43 extraordinary years of remarkable journalism, loyalty and friendship".
"Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I'm very sorry to see her go, but I've come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally," Thompson said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ukraine claims US missile holdup as Trump floats summit without Zelenskyy
Article:
KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the United States on Monday of deliberately delaying the delivery of interceptor missiles to his country, as tensions between Kyiv and Washington escalated over military aid and intelligence-sharing.
Kyiv said it had received no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes, echoing similar claims made last week.
Speaking to US senators on Monday, Zelenskyy said "the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles" already paid for by European countries, and that the shipment was awaiting US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's signature.
He also said several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting US approval.
"The missiles are ready, and they could already be in Ukraine," Zelenskyy said. "But unfortunately, there is still no approval."
The United States has denied making any changes to intelligence-sharing with Ukraine.
Trump has also denied ordering a reduction in speeds on the US government-owned and -controlled Starshield network after Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX developed it, said the order could only have come from the White House.
Strained relations
Relations between the two capitals have been strained since Trump partially lifted sanctions to strike a diesel supply deal with Vladimir Putin and slammed Zelenskyy as a warmonger over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries.
On Monday, Trump defended the diesel deal while once again criticising Zelenskyy.
"Zelenskyy doesn't know what he's talking about," Trump said. "To be honest, I think it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."
Trump also said he was ready to meet Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next month to discuss denuclearisation, adding that the talks could also cover the war in Ukraine — fuelling fears in Kyiv that it was being sidelined.
Earlier in Moscow, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "the topic of such a hypothetical has indeed been mentioned" when asked about a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday that Trump, Putin and Xi could meet.
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said such a meeting would "only encourage Putin to continue this war".
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy also spoke to Pope Leo XIV on Monday, according to the Vatican, days after the Catholic leader held a similar call with Putin.
The Vatican said the Pope had urged both sides to allow aid to flow into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky and civilians to leave.
No information on latest strikes
Russia's latest strikes again hit Ukrainian energy facilities and infrastructure across the country, cutting power to more than 500,000 people and forcing emergency repairs to the battered grid.
"Once again, there was no early warning from our partners," Zelenskyy said as he detailed the damage, deaths and injuries.
Six people, including three children, were killed in a strike near the northeastern city of Kharkiv, the authorities said.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, visiting Uzbekistan on Monday, denied that intelligence-sharing with Ukraine had been withdrawn, backing Trump's call for Zelenskyy to focus on ending the conflict.
Talks to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II remain deadlocked, with Russia refusing to give up its claim to Ukrainian territory and Ukraine steadfastly rejecting attempts to force it to do so.
Trump had vowed to end the war swiftly when he returned to office but has since appeared to tilt towards Russia, including by calling for Zelenskyy to be replaced.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MBSB's transformation faces profitability test
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than seven decades after it began as a building society helping civil servants own homes, MBSB Bhd has evolved into a diversified financial services group.
But turning that transformation into stronger and more sustainable earnings remains a challenge.
Chairman Datuk Wan Kamaruzaman Wan Ahmad acknowledged that legacy financing issues, integration challenges and fierce competition continue to weigh on earnings, despite improvements in the group's funding position and expansion of its financial services.
MBSB's total assets rose 1.5 per cent to RM65.2 billion at the end of 2025 from RM64.3 billion in 2024, its first full financial year following the acquisition of Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd (MIDF).
For Wan Kamaruzaman, who assumed the chairmanship in January 2024, the priority is not simply to expand the group's financing portfolio, but to ensure that growth does not come at the expense of asset quality.
He said shareholders supported management's cautious approach to deploying capital rather than pursuing aggressive financing growth to boost short-term profits.
"The shareholders have more or less agreed with the management that we need to take this very cautiously," he told Business Times in an interview.
He said expanding financing too aggressively could improve profitability in the short term, but risk creating more impaired accounts in the years ahead.
"So the shareholders have felt that we need to do the right thing rather than just expand the books and make the profits," he said.
The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) is MBSB's largest shareholder with a 56.55 per cent stake, followed by Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) with 12.56 per cent, according to Bursa Malaysia data.
Despite these challenges, MBSB has made progress in several areas under its three-year FLIGHT26 transformation programme, which runs from 2024 to 2026.
The strategy focuses on strengthening its funding base, expanding financing, increasing non-funded income and improving operating efficiency.
The group's Casa ratio improved from around six per cent in 2023 to 15.5 per cent at the end of 2025.
Its cost of funds also declined from 3.7 per cent in 2024 to 3.4 per cent last year.
Although MBSB had succeeded in lowering its cost of funds, Wan Kamaruzaman cautioned that aggressive deposit pricing by competing banks could reverse some of those gains.
He said the group considered funding costs below 3.5 per cent comfortable, but some banks were offering rates of around four per cent for corporate deposits.
Such competition, he said, could push MBSB's funding costs above its preferred level.
Meanwhile, non-funded income rose 76 per cent to RM280 million in 2025, reflecting efforts to diversify income sources beyond financing activities.
However, the improvements have yet to translate into stronger overall profitability.
MBSB's net profit fell 31.3 per cent to RM279.5 million in 2025 from RM406.8 million a year earlier.
In the six months ended June 30, 2026, its net profit declined 58.7 per cent to RM74.36 million from RM180.24 million a year earlier.
Its cost-to-income ratio stood at 65.5 per cent as of June 30, compared with 65.8 per cent in the preceding period.
This compares with FLIGHT26's target of 50 per cent by the end of 2026.
THE BURDEN OF LEGACY FINANCING
MBSB's legacy financing challenges can be traced partly to its transition from a housing financier into personal and business financing.
Established in 1950, the institution initially helped civil servants purchase homes at a time when access to housing finance was limited.
But as Malaysia's banking industry developed, commercial banks gained a competitive advantage through their ability to mobilise deposits at lower funding costs.
MBSB, which did not have the same access to deposit funding, gradually diversified into personal financing and lending to small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
Personal loans eventually became the largest segment of MBSB's lending portfolio.
Wan Kamaruzaman said some personal financing facilities offered in the past carried tenures of up to 25 years, creating a mismatch between borrowers' remaining working years and their repayment obligations.
Much of the financing was repaid through salary deductions.
"I think that (to offer such long-tenure financing) is beginning to haunt us a little bit," he said.
In July 2013, Bank Negara Malaysia introduced measures capping personal financing tenures at 10 years, down from the previously permitted 25 years, to curb excessive household debt.
The new limit also applied to MBSB, although financing applications submitted before the measures took effect were unaffected.
The mismatch contributed to non-performing loans that continue to affect the group's asset quality.
MBSB's gross impaired financing ratio improved slightly to 6.23 per cent at the end of June, from 6.33 per cent at the end of 2025. However, this was higher than the 5.33 per cent recorded at the end of 2024.
The group had written off about RM890 million in impaired financing in 2024, contributing to a reduction in its reported impaired financing balance that year.
Another source of impaired financing was MBSB's Ihsan-i personal financing programme under the government's EPF Account 2 Support Facility, introduced to assist individuals facing financial difficulties following the Covid-19 pandemic.
Wan Kamaruzaman acknowledged that financing under the programme had experienced high levels of non-performance, although he said the situation had been managed.
He said reducing the group's overall impaired financing ratio would take time as older facilities matured and were replaced by new financing subject to stricter approval criteria.
MBSB is ultimately targeting a ratio below two per cent, closer to industry levels, said Wan Kamaruzaman.
Construction-related financing has also presented challenges.
Wan Kamaruzaman said some SME borrowers in the sector had been affected by higher funding costs, rising building material prices and increased labour expenses.
MBSB has consequently become more selective in extending construction financing, assessing applications on a case-by-case basis.
The group has also tightened its monitoring of business borrowers by requiring them to maintain operating accounts with the bank, giving it better visibility over their cash flows and financial performance.
INTEGRATION: OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES
Beyond legacy financing, MBSB has undergone two major acquisitions that significantly expanded its business.
The acquisition of Asian Finance Bank, completed in 2018, enabled MBSB to establish a full-fledged Islamic banking operation under Bank Negara's regulatory supervision.
The acquisition of MIDF in 2023 marked another milestone, adding development finance and investment banking capabilities to the group.
Wan Kamaruzaman said the combination had enabled MBSB to offer more comprehensive financial solutions, particularly to SMEs.
Businesses can now access development financing schemes, grants and subsidies alongside conventional banking facilities, allowing MBSB to support their financing requirements at different stages of growth.
But bringing together businesses with different organisational cultures and operating structures has not been straightforward.
Wan Kamaruzaman acknowledged that the integration of MIDF came with difficulties, particularly in aligning employees, reporting requirements and governance structures.
He said the differences had contributed to delays in the cultural integration of the two institutions.
"It's actually an institution of two different cultures coming together. It was not easy," he said.
The group has sought to address these challenges through greater employee engagement, organisational changes and a review of remuneration packages.
Wan Kamaruzaman said MBSB had spent about RM29 million implementing a revised remuneration structure across the group.
Graduate starting salaries have also been raised, while a long-term incentive scheme has been introduced to align employees' interests with the group's profitability and share price performance.
He said attracting and retaining the right talent was essential to bringing the different businesses together.
PREPARING FOR THE NEXT CHAPTER
With FLIGHT26 approaching its conclusion, MBSB is preparing a new four-year strategic plan covering 2027 to 2030.
Wan Kamaruzaman said the group was reviewing its strategic direction with the assistance of external consultants, focusing on improving productivity, operational efficiency and its range of financial products.
He acknowledged that MBSB still has room to improve its turnaround times and offer a broader suite of financial services to customers.
The group is also seeking to expand beyond its traditional customer base of civil servants and corporate clients, with greater emphasis on attracting higher-income customers through digital banking products and other financial solutions.
For an institution that began by financing home ownership before expanding into Islamic banking, development finance and investment banking, the next phase will be about demonstrating the financial benefits of that transformation.
Wan Kamaruzaman said responsible stewardship meant ensuring that the institution was in a stronger position when the time came to hand over its leadership.
Rather than pursuing rapid growth at the risk of accumulating more bad loans, he said the priority is to leave behind a healthier financing portfolio that would allow future management to take the group forward.
For MBSB, the challenge is therefore not merely to grow bigger, but to show that its expanded businesses can deliver stronger returns without repeating the financing problems of the past.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: University of North Carolina settles federal probes by Trump administration
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration has reached a settlement with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill to close 18 federal probes into alleged race discrimination and antisemitism at the university.
Trump has targeted universities with investigations and threats to suspend funding over pro-Palestinian protests against US ally Israel's assault on Gaza, diversity initiatives, transgender policies and climate programmes, raising concerns over free speech, due process and academic freedom.
The voluntary settlement agreement, released by both parties, does not require a monetary payment and will remain in effect until the end of 2028. UNC did not admit to any wrongdoing or liability, and the deal preserves its eligibility for federal funding.
The agreement said UNC would appoint an internal administrator and establish a coordinator position in its compliance office to address discrimination, including antisemitism. It also requires UNC to provide mandatory antisemitism training for students, faculty and staff.
The university said Elizabeth Hall, associate vice-chancellor for university compliance, had been appointed to serve in both roles. She will also act as the point of contact for the Justice Department and oversee UNC's reporting obligations under the deal.
The agreement prohibits face masks or coverings that conceal an individual's identity during protests. It states that student groups "shall be subject to discipline for antisemitic discriminatory conduct".
Trump has alleged that pro-Palestinian protesters are antisemitic and support extremism.
Protesters, including some Jewish groups, say opposing Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories and its assault on Gaza is not antisemitic, and that advocating for Palestinian rights does not imply support for extremism.
A former Justice Department attorney said in a whistleblower complaint in August that the Trump administration's probes of universities over antisemitism allegations lacked evidence and had predetermined outcomes.
The settlement says UNC will adopt and maintain "non-discriminatory" admissions policies and "not use any racial proxy".
It does not prevent UNC from considering how applicants have overcome personal adversity. The university may also consider aspects of family background, such as poverty, provided those considerations are applied consistently, the deal said.
The Justice Department said UNC would submit any complaints of antisemitism and race discrimination it had received to the US Justice and Education departments on a quarterly basis.
The Supreme Court rejected affirmative action at colleges in 2023 when it struck down race-conscious admissions programmes at Harvard and UNC.
Trump has cracked down on diversity initiatives, casting them as discriminatory against white people and men. Civil rights advocates say such initiatives help marginalised groups, including ethnic minorities, LGBT communities and women.
The government has also reached settlements with other universities.
Last year, Columbia University agreed to pay more than US$200 million to the government to resolve investigations, while Brown University said it would pay US$50 million to support local workforce development under a settlement.
Harvard has yet to reach a deal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: As midterms loom, Trump seizes on France unrest for political gain
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump used the protests roiling France to score quick political points on Monday, as the upcoming midterm elections leave his Republican Party facing strong headwinds.
Speaking to reporters, Trump recalled an exchange with his French counterpart Emmanuel Macron: "I told him a long time ago, you're making a big mistake in France. You're letting everybody from the world come in...Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon."
Earlier on Monday, the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform: "The migrants have taken over France. They must CLOSE THE BORDERS, FAST!"
Cost-of-living demonstrations broke out across France over the weekend, with many descending into looting and violent clashes, prompting officials to impose partial curfews on Monday.
While the French protests were inspired by soaring inflation, Trump has framed the violent clashes with police as evidence in favour of the anti-immigration policies he used to successfully campaign for re-election in 2024.
"They're taking this French crisis and turning it into a campaign argument," JC Lintzenich, a senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund think tank, told AFP.
Conservative talking points
Opinion polls heavily favour Trump's rival Democratic Party in the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress.
With just two weeks to go before Americans go to the polls, Trump has seized on any strategy he can to persuade voters to support the Republican Party and his Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement.
"Since the beginning of the MAGA movement, Europe has been an extension of the US political battlefield, so it's not surprising that when there are events like the unrest from October 17, the political machine gets moving," Justin Vaisse, a professor of US foreign policy at Johns Hopkins University, told AFP.
As videos of unrest in France began surfacing on social media, Trump's Vice-President JD Vance wrote on Saturday on X: "Western liberals imported the third world into France...they ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility."
Right-wing US media personalities, including Glenn Beck, Benny Johnson, Nick Sortor and Jack Posobiec, made similar points, blaming immigrants from Muslim-majority countries for causing a crisis in Western identity.
"The riots are viewed as validation of the warnings against immigration in general and Muslim immigration, if such a thing exists," Vaisse said.
Celia Belin, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations and head of its Paris office, views the commentary as an "export of domestic policies" by a US administration that openly supports nationalist parties in Europe.
She told AFP that Trump and his allies "rushed into this argument, the same one that Vance had presented in Munich" in 2025, in a controversial speech described as a US culture war against Europe, with the goal of "fanning the flames".
Polling priorities
Experts note that this rhetorical strategy, while it may have succeeded in 2024, is not necessarily what US voters want to hear these days.
"When you look at the campaign ads here – I'm in South Carolina right now – it's about healthcare, domestic issues," Lintzenich said.
"The international element is a blip on the radar, and Ukraine, and Iran, and other ongoing national security issues rate higher than the current French instability," he continued.
A Pew Research poll this month found that the economy plays an important role in the choice of 82 per cent of US voters, far more than immigration (59 per cent) or race-related issues (36 per cent).
Though Trump has followed through on his 2024 campaign promise to crack down on immigration, he has been less successful in delivering on his pledge to curb inflation, with his tariff policies and war with Iran driving up prices across the economy and pushing his approval rating to record lows.
Vaisse said linking US identitarian rhetoric to events in France "is not going to win a single vote" for Republicans, though it could "mobilise the base" to vote.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australian lawmaker hurt in car attack underwent surgery overnight
Article:
WANGARATTA: Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines underwent surgery overnight but remains in a critical condition after being deliberately struck by a car, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday.
Political violence is rare in Australia, but law enforcement agencies have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed at the nation's elected officials in recent years.
Albanese said the attack was a "test of our character" and prompted an outpouring of support for Haines, who has been widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.
She was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200km northeast of Melbourne, at around 3.35pm (0435 GMT) on Monday.
Witnesses told national broadcaster ABC they heard a bang and saw a woman pinned between two cars.
She was retrieving items from the boot of her car when the attack happened, Albanese said.
The driver made a U-turn to get back to her after passing, he added.
"It's clear this was a deliberate act," he said.
[[nid:1559384]]
'Hero' barber
The 65-year-old was critically injured.
She underwent surgery overnight at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne.
"Helen remains in hospital in a critical condition. I spoke with her husband Phil last night, and she underwent surgery last night," Albanese told Australian breakfast show Sunrise on Tuesday.
"All Australians' thoughts are with the family, with her many friends, with her community," he added.
The 43-year-old male driver was restrained by local barber Ricky Jefferies, who is now widely hailed as a "hero".
He told journalists his first thought had been: "My wife would be disappointed if I'm injured."
"My family, they're everything, and my community is second to that," a visibly shaken Jefferies told journalists.
"The other people here were just, they did so much more than me... they deserve the credit."
The driver was then arrested by police, who found a knife in his car.
Australian media reported that he was known to police.
The investigation is ongoing.
[[nid:1559383]]
'Devastating'
The alleged attacker's motive remains unknown, and Albanese has refused to speculate while the investigation is ongoing.
However, he has lamented that political debate in Australia had become too heated and personal in recent years, pointing to a significant increase in threats against elected officials.
"It's important in a democracy that people are allowed to have disagreements," he said.
"But that doesn't mean that you have to draw into question people's motivations or their patriotism or who they are."
"We've seen, I think, political discourse go in the wrong direction in recent times," he said.
Victoria Premier Ben Carroll said he was "appalled" by the "violent attack" in his state.
"I know how devastating this will be for the Wangaratta community and all those who Helen represents," he said.
Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife. She became known for positions including support for stronger climate action.
"This afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care," her family said.
"We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response."
Tributes to the independent lawmaker have poured in from across the political spectrum.
Conservative opposition leader Angus Taylor described it as a "shocking day for our nation".
Far-right Senator Pauline Hanson said "violence against any elected representative, whoever they are and whatever they stand for, is never acceptable in Australia".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Posh cars put Kempas PPR tenants in spotlight [WATCH]
Article:
JOHOR BARU: At least four tenants of a low-cost public housing scheme in Johor have come under scrutiny after being found to own luxury cars, raising questions over their eligibility for subsidised homes intended for lower-income households.
The tenants live at the People's Housing Programme (PPR) project in Kempas, where a recent enforcement operation by the Johor State Housing Development Corporation (PKPJ) uncovered their vehicle ownership.
One of the vehicles was a MINI John CooperWorks sports model worth nearly RM400,000.
Johor has 15,631 affordable rental homes under 14 PPR projects and eight Government Rental Housing (RSK) projects, managed by PKPJ for lower-income households.
PKPJ chief executive officer Datin Paduka Dr Suhailizan Suliman said the cases were uncovered during investigations into vehicle ownership among public housing tenants.
[[nid:1559377]]
"We are reviewing vehicle ownership data and conducting fresh profiling of tenants to assess whether they still meet the eligibility criteria, including those found to own luxury vehicles."
However, she stressed that owning a luxury vehicle did not automatically constitute a breach of the rules.
"Every case will undergo checks and verification before further action is taken in accordance with the applicable rules and procedures."
She said remedial notices had been issued to the four tenants, who would undergo further checks to determine eligibility.
The findings have raised questions over whether subsidised homes are reaching those who need them, as thousands of Johoreans continue to depend on affordable rental housing.
Suhailizan said PKPJ was stepping up enforcement against the misuse of PPR and RSK units to ensure eligible low-income families had fair access.
Since the beginning of this year, about 1,453 remedial notices had been issued over rental arrears. A further 348 termination notices and 55 eviction notices were issued after tenants ignored remedial notices.
Enforcement efforts had also targeted illegal subletting and tenants who left their units vacant, denying other eligible families access to affordable homes, she said.
"Subletting is a serious offence," she told the New Straits Times.
The public housing projects are intended to provide affordable rental homes for the B40 group, comprising the bottom 40 per cent of households by income and generally including lower-income families eligible for targeted government assistance.
"So far, we have issued remedial notices to 68 tenants for illegally subletting their PPR and RSK units, with 47 served termination and eviction notices."
Suhailizan said PKPJ had also issued 812 remedial notices to tenants who failed to occupy their units or left them vacant. Of these, 328 received termination and eviction notices.
Of the cases involving vacant units, 89 tenants were confirmed not to be occupying their homes, prompting eviction operations.
She said enforcement was carried out through periodic inspections, public complaints and cooperation with the management bodies of PPR and RSK projects.
She warned that PKPJ would not compromise on proven violations, including unauthorised subletting, leaving units vacant and other breaches.
"The housing provided by the Johor government is assistance for those who genuinely need it, not something to be misused for personal gain.
"Many Johoreans are still in need of a home. We must not deny them the opportunity by abusing the facilities provided by the state government," she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump calls for renaming New Mexico 'New America'
Article:
ISTANBUL: US President Donald Trump on Monday called for the southwestern state of New Mexico to be renamed "New America", arguing that the change would boost its prestige, property values and incomes, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
"New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America. We are not Mexico, we are the United States of America!" Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
"The name would add great value and prestige to the State! Home Values and Incomes would rise, and you would be even prouder while saluting our beautiful American Flag!" he added.
The president first proposed the name change in September, describing "New America" as a more prestigious name for New Mexico, a landlocked state in the US Southwest.
However, Trump cannot unilaterally rename a US state, as changing New Mexico's name would require amending its constitution. The state's Democratic governor, Michelle Lujan Grisham, rejected the proposal when he first raised it last month.
The suggestion follows Trump's earlier efforts to rename geographical landmarks, including his January 2025 executive order directing US federal authorities to adopt "Gulf of America" in place of Gulf of Mexico.
In August, he signed another executive order directing US federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario, which borders the US and Canada, as "Lake America".
Trump also floated renaming the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean "Trump Ocean" or "Ocean of the Americas" during an October 10 rally in Tennessee.
More recently, during a rally in Georgia on Friday, Trump claimed he had jokingly asked Google about renaming the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean "Trump Ocean".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US set to announce certification of Boeing 737 MAX 10 on Tuesday
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is expected to announce on Tuesday that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has approved the Boeing 737 MAX 10 during a visit to Washington state, sources briefed on the plans told Reuters.
Duffy is set to appear at a Boeing factory in Everett, Washington, to announce the FAA certification of the long-delayed larger variant of Boeing's best-selling aircraft.
Boeing opened a new production line at the Everett plant in July to expand 737 MAX production. The aircraft is also assembled in Renton.
Boeing referred questions to the FAA, which did not immediately comment.
The FAA conducted a review by its Type Certification Board on Friday. The board comprises FAA management team members and its review is a final step before the agency decides on certification.
Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for about 30 per cent of Boeing's outstanding 737 backlog. The planemaker has already built a handful of MAX 10s awaiting delivery.
The larger aircraft, which can carry more passengers, is crucial to several airlines' growth plans. Major customers for the MAX 10 include United Airlines, Alaska Airlines, Ryanair, Delta Air Lines and American Airlines.
Boeing has faced a more stringent certification process since two fatal MAX 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019, as well as scrutiny of its production and quality systems following a mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9 in January 2024.
Duffy met the chief executives of major aerospace companies, including Boeing, RTX, Honeywell, GE Aerospace, Textron and Gulfstream, in Georgia last week to discuss how the certification process could be improved.
The FAA gave long-awaited approval to the smaller 737 MAX 7 in August after reviewing the aircraft for more than eight years. Before the delays, Boeing had initially planned to begin delivering the MAX 10 in 2020.
A problem with the anti-ice system on 737 MAX engines that emerged in 2023 further delayed certification of the MAX 7 and MAX 10.
A glitch in the latest update to the 737 MAX's navigation software threatened to delay certification further when Boeing disclosed it in late September.
However, the FAA determined that it did not pose a safety concern and did not require Boeing to fix the problem as a condition of certifying the aircraft.
Boeing is still working to certify the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production, which is already six years behind schedule. The company has said it expects to complete certification and begin deliveries in 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid calls for cabinet paper on motorcycle safety
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE Transport Ministry and the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (Miros) will prepare a cabinet paper on motorcycle safety, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
"I call upon the Transport Ministry, together with Miros, to prepare a joint cabinet paper proposing a coordinated national approach to expand proven motorcycle safety measures, with clear priorities, timelines and measurable outcomes."
Zahid was speaking at the Conference on Asia Road Safety (CARS) 2026, held with Transport Expo Asia 2026, organised by Miros here.
He also called for an integrated national road safety intelligence platform to link data systems across relevant agencies and to improve coordination.
He said the government, industry, schools and communities must work together to foster a national culture of road safety, adding that awareness alone was insufficient to change risky behaviour.
Zahid said Malaysia must strengthen coordination and sustain road safety efforts to achieve its target of reducing road fatalities by 50 per cent by 2030.
He said motorcyclists accounted for the largest share of road fatalities in Malaysia, underscoring the need for safer roads, better infrastructure and effective policies.
"Too often, we place the blame on riders and their behaviour. While personal responsibility is important, road safety must work both ways.
"We need responsible riders, but we must also provide safer roads, better infrastructure and effective policies," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says Washington golf course project to start immediately, despite judge's order
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration would begin renovation work immediately on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior notification to the court.
The renovation work, which Trump said a day earlier would start next month, has become the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns.
In a Monday morning post on Truth Social, Trump blasted the judge as "a crazed lunatic", called the court case "ridiculous" and declared that his administration had "an absolute right" to proceed.
"The experts at 'Interior' are allowed to do this First Class renovation 'as of right.' They do not need an approval. Work is scheduled to begin IMMEDIATELY!" he wrote.
It was unclear how the judge would respond.
The renovation is among multiple projects Trump is pursuing to reshape the White House and other Washington landmarks.
US District Judge Ana Reyes ruled earlier this year that the government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the golf course could proceed. Last week, she issued an order halting the removal of trees at the site, which she called "inexcusable".
In a post on Sunday, Trump said work on the East Potomac Golf Links would begin on November 15 and that the course would reopen in about 15 months.
Earlier this year, he said work would begin in September.
[[nid:1559363]]
Later on Sunday, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to explain whether it maintained its position, argued last week, that there was "no final agency action" regarding the course and that, at most, "the President has given preliminary thought" to the renovations.
Responding to the judge's order, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward wrote in a filing that any redesign of the golf course was not an "agency action".
"Just as a decision to redesign all the art exhibits in a Smithsonian Museum would not be agency action, neither would a decision to redesign a golf course, or to trim trees, replace fences, expand the fairways, or mow the lawn," Woodward wrote.
The DC Preservation League filed a lawsuit in February to halt the administration's takeover of the golf course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history".
In an Oct 9 court filing, the Trump administration had asked Reyes to dismiss the litigation, saying it was premature because the "proposed project remains at an early and conceptual stage".
The next day, however, the government removed about 500 trees from the site, saying the work would improve safety at the park, restore its original design and form part of a 2019 plan that predated Trump's ambitions for the course. Reyes ordered the removals to stop.
On Friday, the government filed a motion to disqualify Reyes and transfer the case to another district judge, saying her actions had shown "deep-seated and unequivocal antipathy toward the Trump Administration", according to court records.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tiger footprints found at Perak farm
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE Perak Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has confirmed the discovery of tiger footprints at a farm near Jalan Air Betang-Jalan Kampung Air Panas, Gerik, last Wednesday.
"Initial field investigations indicate that the report is credible, as tiger footprints were indeed found.
"The orchard is about 2km from the Bintang Hijau Forest Reserve," said Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah yesterday.
Images of the footprints have gone viral, raising concerns among residents.
Pazil said Perhilitan was conducting regular checks in the area and gathering information from residents and farmers.
He advised them to remain vigilant, avoid going out alone in the early morning, late evening or at night, and keep livestock in secure enclosures.
"People are also advised not to provoke, approach or attempt to track the animal.
"Any sightings should be reported immediately to the department through the official complaint channels."
