Title: Johor JPJ collects RM1.17m in VEP summonses from January to October
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — The Johor Road Transport Department (JPJ) issued 7,804 summonses totalling RM1.17 million through the implementation of the Vehicle Entry Permit (VEP) from January to October 18, according to its director Zulkarnain Yasin.
He said this was the result of inspections on 120,740 vehicles at the state’s two land entry points — the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) and Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB).
He said enforcement operations were conducted continuously at the two entry points.
“However, the rate of non-compliance among foreign drivers is actually still low compared with the overall number of vehicles inspected,” he said in an interview with Bernama recently.
He said JPJ mobile vans had been stationed at BSI and KSAB since early this month to facilitate the payment of VEP summonses.
He said that so far, no foreign vehicles had been barred from leaving the country through the two entry points for failing to pay summonses.
“Our action is to prevent summonses from accumulating. Automatically, they (vehicle owners) have to pay on the spot, which is why we have also provided a mobile squad,” he said.
He said his team was always on standby at the locations to ensure smooth operations in the event of technical issues or disruptions to the VEP system.
Zulkarnain said that although full enforcement of the VEP had been implemented last year, some foreign vehicle owners still claimed that they were unaware of the requirement.
“Some of them say they did not know, even though it (VEP enforcement) has been in place for a long time. We will not accept such excuses,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia targets Smart Highway technology on half of expressways in the country, says works minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysia aims to equip at least 50 per cent of its 34 expressways with Smart Highway technology to enhance road safety, improve traffic flow and boost transport system efficiency.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the initiative would incorporate artificial intelligence (AI), smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, and detection and early-warning systems for high-risk incidents, including accidents.
Other features include solar-powered lighting, digital mobility applications and electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure.
“Malaysia is also prioritising the development of a National Intelligent Traffic Management Centre (NITMC) to strengthen real-time monitoring, integrated data analysis and traffic management coordination.
“Another key component is the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection system, which allows vehicles to pass through toll plazas without stopping at barriers, thereby reducing congestion and saving travel time,” he said in a statement issued by the Ministry of Works (KKR) yesterday.
Nanta highlighted the initiative during his address at a high-level roundtable session held in conjunction with the 2026 Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) World Congress in Gangneung, South Korea, from October 19 to 23.
Themed “Beyond Mobility, Connected World”, the congress brings together about 60,000 participants from around 90 countries to discuss innovations and future developments in intelligent transport systems.
On the implementation of the initiatives, Nanta said the government was allowing highway concessionaires and industry partners to refine a business-to-business (B2B) model under the regulatory oversight of the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA).
He said the approach took into account technological and commercial viability, system interoperability, payment integration, data security and consumer protection.
“The current focus is on finalising the technical, operational and legal preparations before the proposal is submitted to the government for consideration and final approval,” the statement said.
Meanwhile, Nanta held a bilateral meeting with the Republic of Korea’s Second Vice-Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Jeong Eui-kyung, to strengthen cooperation in infrastructure development, construction technology and intelligent transport systems.
Speaking to the Malaysian media after the meeting, Nanta said both countries discussed ways to enhance cooperation in road and highway infrastructure development, including the adoption of new technologies and more efficient management methods.
He said the meeting also reviewed progress in implementing cooperation under a memorandum of understanding (MoU) previously signed between the MHA and the Korea Expressway Corporation (KEC).
“During the bilateral meeting, we reviewed what has been achieved and discussed how cooperation between the two countries could be further strengthened, particularly in the road and highway development industry and the application of the latest technologies and methods,” he said.
Nanta added that the collaboration would continue, with the MHA and KEC scheduled to hold a follow-up session today to further strengthen their partnership in highway infrastructure development. — Bernama

Title: Hamzah expects Anwar to call GE16 by August next year amid Pakatan-Umno tensions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin expects Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to call the 16th general election by August next year, citing growing tensions between Pakatan Harapan and Umno, according to
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT).
Speaking in an interview with
BFM Radio,
Hamzah said the unity government might struggle to remain intact beyond 2027, pointing to renewed scrutiny of Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s court cases by PH lawmakers.
Hamzah, who leads Wawasan, suggested that the growing friction between the two political blocs could prompt Anwar to call an election before the coalition government fractures.
“I think they have already started to break up. So he has to call (for an election) before that,” he was quoted as saying.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers decided in January to take no further action on 47 charges involving corruption, criminal breach of trust and money laundering against Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional chairman.
The decision drew criticism from DAP leaders, FMT reported.
Hamzah also suggested Anwar could capitalise on the 2027 SEA Games to build public support before calling an election immediately after the sporting event, scheduled for September 18 to 29.
“Whether it will happen or not, I don’t know. I’m not very sure about that,” he said, as reported by FMT.
He also pointed to the 2027 Budget, which he said contained numerous benefits for the public, as well as a substantial increase in funding for the Election Commission, as possible indications that a general election was approaching.
The EC’s allocation under the recently tabled 2027 Budget rose to RM367 million, compared with RM167 million allocated the previous year.
The next general election must be held by February 2028. Anwar said last month that he was open to considering calls for an early election.

Title: Temerloh police bust four gangs linked to ECRL, TM cable thefts in Pahang
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 20 — Police have crippled four gangs suspected of robbing and stealing cables belonging to the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) and Telekom Malaysia (TM) in operations conducted from October 12 until yesterday around Temerloh and Mentakab.
Temerloh police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said in a statement that between September and October this year, two robbery cases at ECRL cable storage facilities and five TM cable theft cases were reported around Temerloh, Mentakab, and Lanchang.
He said 17 local men aged between 20 and 60 were arrested during the operations, with total losses incurred by ECRL and TM estimated at RM75,000.
“The first group, known as Geng Ravi, was crippled through operations from October 12 to October 15. Investigations revealed the gang is also believed to be involved in several iron and cable theft cases at project sites and factories abandoned by their owners since July this year, while police are tracking down two other suspects who remain at large,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said on October 14, police crippled Geng Kepala, believed to be involved in several Tenaga Nasional Berhad cable thefts at storage facilities, factories, and roadsides around Mentakab since August.
Mohd Nasyim said police arrested a 28-year-old man believed to be a member of Geng Dany in Mentakab yesterday for suspected TM cable theft, adding the gang was previously active in similar activities around Kuala Lumpur.
“The suspect confessed to involvement in several TM cable thefts along roadsides around Mentakab since October this year, alongside another accomplice still at large,” he said.
In an early-morning operation yesterday, he said the department crippled Geng Mista, believed to have been involved in several TM cable thefts from manholes and roadside poles around Temerloh, Mentakab, Jerantut, and Maran since July.
“The gang leader was identified as a member of Geng Kepala arrested on October 14, while another suspect remains at large,” he said.
He said police seized several vehicles, including a lorry, along with coils and cut cable pieces belonging to ECRL, TNB, and TM. They also seized cut iron pole pieces and tools believed to have been used to steal and process cables.
Mohd Nasyim said all suspects were detained to assist in investigations under Section 395 and Section 379 of the Penal Code, Section 431A of the Penal Code, and Section 235(2) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. — Bernama

Title: Babysitter detained after 10-month-old baby boy dies in her care in Tasek Gelugor
Article:
TASEK GELUGOR, Oct 20 — Police have detained a babysitter to assist in investigations into the death of a 10-month-old baby boy who was reported to have died while in the woman’s care here yesterday.
Seberang Perai Utara district police chief ACP Anuar Abdul Rahman said the woman was detained following the incident and the case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
“Investigations are ongoing, and we are waiting for the post-mortem report to find out the actual cause of the baby’s death,” he said in a statement last night.
It is understood that the baby’s mother sent him to the babysitter early this morning.
The 25-year-old babysitter allegedly found the baby weak and lethargic at about 9.50 am and took him to a nearby clinic.
The baby is believed to have died before arriving at the clinic. Preliminary physical examinations reportedly found no visible bruising on his body. — Bernama

Title: Penang police arrest six men over alleged abuse of Indonesian woman in Selangor
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Oct 20 — Police have detained six men to assist investigations into the abuse of an Indonesian woman in Tanjong Sepat, Selangor, in a raid at a business premise at Pusat Perniagaan Oren, Jalan Merbau, here today.
Seberang Perai Utara district police chief ACP Anuar Abdul Rahman said the 6.30pm raid was carried out by the Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) Criminal Investigation Department (CID) team, with assistance from the Penang IPK CID team.
“The raid was conducted following an incident on October 16, in which an Indonesian woman sustained burns to her body after she was allegedly abused by her employer at Jalan Besar Kampung Tumbok, Tanjong Sepat.
“The victim has been rescued. Following the incident, police detained six men, including the woman’s employer, to assist in investigations into the case,” he said in a statement tonight.
He said further investigations are ongoing and the case is being investigated under Section 12 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM) [Act 670].
Earlier, several videos and photographs alleging a murder at Pusat Perniagaan Oren went viral following the presence of police vehicles at the location, causing concern among the public. — Bernama

Title: Data centres’ power demand to hit 8.39GW by 2030, with Johor accounting for biggest share
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Peak electricity demand from the data centre industry in Peninsular Malaysia is projected to reach 8.39 gigawatts (GW) by 2030, based on the current electricity supply planning estimates, according to the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra).
Of the total amount, Johor is expected to record the highest demand for electricity at 4.42GW, and Selangor at 1.48GW.
“Both states are major hubs for data centre development and will therefore require proper electricity supply infrastructure planning that takes into account the anticipated growth in demand,” it said.
The ministry was responding to a question from Onn Abu Bakar (PH-Batu Pahat) on the projected electricity and water demand by the data centre industry up to 2030, particularly in Johor and Selangor, as well as the number of data centres that have been completed.
Petra said 45 data centres had been completed and were operational in Peninsular Malaysia as of August 2026, with a combined electricity supply capacity of 6.04GW.
This capacity refers to the electricity supply provided by Tenaga Nasional Bhd through the National Grid to support the operation of the data centres.
Meanwhile, the projected water demand from data centres in Selangor and Johor is expected to reach 389.04 million litres per day (MLD) by 2030.
“However, actual water consumption by data centres currently reported to the National Water Services Commission stands at 63.90 MLD,” Petra said. — Bernama

Title: Lunas targets April 2027 delivery of first littoral combat ship to Royal Malaysian Navy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Lumut Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd (Lunas) remains committed to delivering the first littoral combat ship (LCS1) to the Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN), with the target for physical delivery revised to April 2027.
Lunas said the revised delivery timeline for LCS1 should be viewed in the context of the programme’s overall technical, regulatory and contractual complexities, and the ship’s delivery schedule was affected by the cancellation of the export licence for the surface-to-surface missile system by the Norwegian authorities as well.
Following the decision, Lunas was no longer permitted under international export control regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), to deliver a ship equipped with the missile launcher system in question.
Lunas said it had formally informed the Defence Ministry (Mindef) of the technical, cost and scheduling implications arising from the development, which fell outside the scope and control of the company’s original contract.
The company also explained that several critical complementary contracts required for physical delivery were not included in Lunas’ existing scope and had to be contracted directly by Mindef with the original equipment manufacturers.
In addition, the Letter of Acceptance (LoA) for the Integrated Logistics Support and Test Assistance package was issued in August 2025, but the contract was only finalised and signed in August 2026.
Lunas said the delay had affected the implementation of the training programme, which formed an important part of the package’s scope.
On the proposed imposition of Liquidated and Ascertained Damages (LAD), Lunas said any determination of contractual responsibility must be made through the prescribed contractual and legal mechanisms, and that the Auditor-General’s Report should not be regarded as a final determination of contractual liability.
The company said the audit was conducted based on information provided by Mindef and the RMN, while respecting the report’s findings and recommendations.
Lunas reaffirmed its commitment to delivering an LCS that is safe, capable and mission-ready to strengthen the RMN’s operational readiness. However, the target for physical delivery in April 2027 could be pushed back further if the Contract Variation Order continued to be delayed. — Bernama

Title: Nearly RM11b in STR, Sara aid disbursed as of September, says Finance Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Nearly RM11 billion in Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) assistance had been disbursed to eligible recipients as of September 2026, according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
MoF said that RM3.6 billion had been disbursed to STR recipients through three payment phases as of last month.
The ministry said the government continues to ensure that the RM15 billion allocated for STR and Sara in 2026 delivers tangible benefits to the people, especially low-income groups and vulnerable communities.
“This year, nearly nine million citizens are eligible to receive Sara monthly, while STR is distributed quarterly to eligible households and the elderly.
“The effectiveness of the implementation of STR and Sara can be accessed through several aspects, including recipient coverage, aid utilisation, targeting accuracy and the ability of the aid to meet basic needs,” it said in a written response published on the Parliament website.
MoF said this in response to Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s (PN-Pagoh) question regarding the effectiveness of the RM15 billion allocation for STR and Sara based on basic spending and its distribution to low-income citizens.
The ministry noted that the monthly Sara recorded a utilisation rate of 99.7 per cent, with a transaction value of RM5.2 billion as of September 2026.
Meanwhile, for Sara Untuk Semua, more than 20 million citizens had made purchases, representing 90 per cent of the total number of recipients, with transaction values in the local market amounting to nearly RM1.9 billion, it added. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry says no commitment to bail out AirAsia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Finance Ministry (MoF) has not made any commitment to provide financial assistance to AirAsia Bhd, whether in the form of guarantees, financing or injection of public funds.
The ministry said applications for government support from any companies will be considered based on the interests of the country and the people, fiscal sustainability and the protection of public funds, in accordance with prevailing laws and procedures.
It also said the government will not comment on any speculation or figures reported by the media to avoid affecting the market and the interests of employees, customers and other stakeholders of the companies concerned.
“The government will continue to monitor the developments closely, while prioritising the people’s interest,” it said in a written reply to the Dewan Rakyat, published on the Parliament’s website.
The MoF was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong (BN-Ayer Hitam) on whether the government is considering providing any guarantees, loans or public funds to AirAsia.
The ministry said the government has taken note of issues raised concerning AirAsia, including the losses reported in its latest quarterly financial results.
The airline had mainly attributed its losses to the spike in jet fuel prices due to the West Asia conflict.
“The government regularly engages with players across the aviation industry as part of its monitoring efforts, to seek input from industry players, technical experts and other parties, as it has also done for other economic sectors affected by the West Asia crisis,” it said.
On September 19, Bernama reported that AirAsia had not held any discussions with the government on a “bailout” and remained confident in its liquidity position and business sustainability. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Govt refining haze plan, reviewing school closure measures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is refining proposals to improve the National Haze Action Plan, particularly regarding school closure directives and the Ministry of Education’s (MOE) early preparations to ensure learning can continue if schools are forced to close.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, via a Facebook post yesterday, said the health of children remains the government’s top priority while ensuring their education is not disrupted.
He said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Department of Environment, and the Malaysian Meteorological Department will refine these proposals together with the MOE and the Ministry of Health (MOH).
“I also emphasised that allocation requirements for cloud seeding operations will be fulfilled to reduce the haze. These operations are currently being carried out almost daily, depending on suitable cloud conditions,” he said in the post.
Earlier, the Prime Minister chaired a National Disaster Management Council meeting, which discussed in detail the current and concerning haze situation as well as its impact on public health, especially school going children.
Anwar said the meeting was also briefed on the country’s preparations to face the North-east Monsoon, which is expected to bring heavy rain and flood risks, as well as the threat of a Super El Nino forecasted to bring extreme hot and dry weather next year.
“Accordingly, the preparedness of frontline agencies must continue to be enhanced. Nadma must be empowered as the pulse of cross-agency policy and operational coordination, particularly through the Central Disaster Operations Control Centre, so that prevention, preparation, response, and recovery measures can be implemented swiftly and effectively,” he said.
He added that the Federal and State Governments, the private sector, volunteers, and the community must move together to strengthen community preparedness.
“The lives of the people must be protected, and aid must reach those in need immediately. This is the trust that we must shoulder together,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Firefly to fully resume Subang-Singapore flights on Oct 22
Article:
SINGAPORE, Oct 20 — Firefly will fully resume its flights between Subang and Singapore on Thursday (October 22), following its latest operational assessment of weather and haze conditions in Singapore.
In an advisory on Monday, the airline said it would operate a reduced flight schedule between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport on October 21 before restoring full services the following day.
“Affected passengers are being contacted and offered alternative travel arrangements on available Malaysia Airlines flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Singapore (SIN), subject to seat availability.
“Passengers who choose not to proceed with the alternative arrangements are eligible for a full refund,” it said.
The wholly owned subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines had earlier cancelled all scheduled flights between the two airports up until Monday.
The flights scheduled to resume on October 21 are FY3122 and FY3123, FY3126 and FY3127, and FY3130 and FY3131.
Singapore’s air quality improved on Monday, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) ranging from 86 to 115 as of 11pm, according to the National Environment Agency (NEA). — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: ‘Corporate mafia’, Felda abuse of power claims among issues to be raised
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Allegations of “corporate mafia” activities and abuse of power involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) are among the issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official portal, during Minister’s Question Time, Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) will ask the Prime Minister for an update on “corporate mafia” allegations involving violations of the law and the action taken so far.
Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) will ask the Prime Minister for an update on investigations into alleged misappropriation, corruption and abuse of power involving Felda, including its subsidiary Felda Investment Corporation.
The question-and-answer session will follow, with Datuk Dr Nik Muhammad Zawawi Salleh (PN-Pasir Puteh) seeking details from the Economy Minister on the policy indicators, quantitative targets and timelines under the 13th Malaysia Plan to address development disparities between districts.
Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng) will also ask the Agriculture and Food Security Minister about the outcomes of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition 2026, as well as the added value and follow-up investments expected to materialise from the memoranda of understanding signed.
Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) will ask the Prime Minister whether the government is prepared to make merit-based appointments free from political influence, a key governance policy for Tabung Haji, in line with one of the Royal Commission of Inquiry's recommendations.
The sitting is scheduled to continue with the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill (Budget 2027), following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9.
The calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament shows that the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 is scheduled for October 12 to 22, with the relevant ministers to wind up the debate over four days from October 26.
The Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to sit for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: In haze-hit Johor, staying indoors is a luxury delivery riders cannot afford
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — For delivery riders in Johor, escaping the thick haze that has settled over the state is not as simple as staying indoors. Their livelihoods depend on being out on the road, even as the polluted air takes a toll on their health.
As air quality reached very unhealthy levels in several parts of the state last week, riders reported sore throats, stinging eyes and other symptoms, leaving some to weigh the cost of fewer deliveries against the risks of prolonged exposure.
The haze, carried across the region by smoke from fires in Indonesia, has prompted Johor to extend school and educational institution closures until October 23, even as outdoor workers continue their daily routines.
For Ghani Jaafar, a 50-year-old food and beverage delivery rider on the outskirts of Johor Bahru, the effects of the haze were difficult to ignore.
After spending long hours making deliveries on his motorcycle, he developed a sore throat and mild nasal irritation.
“The symptoms happened early last week and persisted up till the weekend.
“If the haze becomes severe this week, I will consider temporarily scaling down on my deliveries,” he told
Malay Mail
while making his rounds yesterday.
Delivery rider Ghani Jaafar, 50, said he experienced a sore throat and nasal irritation after prolonged exposure to the haze in Johor last week. — Picture by Ben Tan
But cutting back on work is hardly straightforward.
Ghani also works part-time as a construction site supervisor, leaving him with little opportunity to escape the outdoor conditions. Between the two jobs, he spends more than 10 hours a day working.
“It is meaningless for people like me to be indoors as both my jobs are based outdoors. On average, I spend more than 10 hours a day doing both jobs.
“The best I can do is to drink more water, monitor the current Air Pollutant Index (API) and try to minimise being outdoors,” he said.
He is aware of the risks, from coughing and eye irritation to sore throats and shortness of breath. Yet avoiding the haze would also mean giving up working hours.
Prolonged exposure to haze, particularly fine particulate matter known as PM2.5, can irritate the eyes and respiratory tract and aggravate existing conditions such as asthma.
In an October 15 advisory, the Health Ministry urged the public to avoid outdoor activities when the API exceeds 100, the threshold for unhealthy air quality, and recommended N95 masks for those who must venture outside. Employers were also advised to provide the masks to outdoor workers.
Part-time delivery rider Mohd Eddin Sanusi, 38, called on the government to provide financial assistance to gig workers affected by the haze in Johor. — Picture by Ben Tan
For Mohd Eddin Sanusi, another delivery rider, the problem has been particularly acute on the road.
The 38-year-old said the haze had left his eyes sore and stinging, sometimes affecting his ability to see clearly while riding his motorcycle.
“Since early last week, I have had sore eyes that started with a stinging sensation from the haze.
“This also affected my vision when I’m riding my motorcycle,” he told
Malay Mail
when met at a 24-hour restaurant here recently.
“I wash my face more often and use eye drops to relieve the soreness.
“Besides that, I was advised by my family to avoid any delivery runs if the API is above 200,” said Mohd Eddin, who also works as a car rental executive in Pontian.
Under Malaysia’s API classification, readings between 201 and 300 are considered very unhealthy, while those above 300 are classified as hazardous.
Johor recorded 30,648 cases of asthma and upper respiratory tract infections in October as of mid-month, a 20.7 per cent week-on-week increase, according to state Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali.
Mohd Eddin began making deliveries three years ago to supplement his income. He described the latest haze as the worst he had encountered since taking up the work.
“This time round, the haze has hit most of southern Johor, where most delivery riders are based.
“It would be good if the government could come out with an assistance package for gig workers like me who are affected by the haze,” he said.
For some riders, the trade-off is already reshaping their working routines.
Delivery rider Putera Mohammad Aidil, 41 (3rd left), has turned to an air quality monitoring app to track haze conditions and plan his daily deliveries in Johor. — Picture courtesy of Putera Mohammad Aidil
Putera Mohammad Aidil, 41, who makes food deliveries for his family’s stall in Bandar Baru Uda, has begun limiting how far he travels after experiencing a sore throat and eye irritation.
The Johor Bahru-based rider said he was concerned about the long-term consequences of breathing polluted air while working.
He recently downloaded an air quality monitoring app to help plan his daily deliveries, but it was advice from his wife that led him to restrict his routes to nearby residential areas.
“My family operates a food stall in Bandar Baru Uda and I normally do the motorcycle deliveries,” he said when contacted yesterday.
“With the current haze and due to health concerns, my wife told me to concentrate my deliveries within the nearby residential area only.
“In a way, this cuts down on my deliveries and contact with the haze, but it also affects my business as well.
“However, as a family man with three young children, I can’t forgo my health.”

Title: Not sympathy, but opportunity: Push grows for fairer hiring of visually impaired Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — It is not a lack of talent, but rather stigma and doubts about their capabilities that continue to hinder persons with visual impairments from entering the job market, including the creative arts industry.
With advances in technology and the availability of assistive facilities, they are capable of using computers and smartphones and carrying out various tasks independently, depending on their skills and the suitability of the job.
Malaysian Association for the Blind (MAB) chief executive officer Datuk George Thomas told Bernama that misconceptions among employers about the capabilities of persons with visual impairments remained prevalent, undermining their chances of securing jobs based on their qualifications and talents.
He said more than half of the 41 employers who attended the Advocacy and Awareness Programme on Employment for Persons with Visual Impairments on June 30 did not know that members of the group could independently use computers and smartphones.
The programme, organised by MAB in collaboration with the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), aimed to raise employers’ awareness of the actual capabilities of persons with visual impairments.
“Some employers assume that if they hire a person with a visual impairment, they need to provide an assistant to help them, whereas MAB has taught persons with visual impairments to live independently. We do not want them to be given opportunities out of sympathy, but because they are qualified or genuinely talented,” he said.
Perkeso deputy chief executive (Operations) Azirruan Arifin said employers’ doubts about the capabilities of persons with visual impairments remained a challenge in efforts to place them in the job market, even when they possessed the relevant academic qualifications, skills and experience.
He said successful job placement also depended on the suitability of the position and the working environment, including physical accessibility, digital systems, screen-reading software and appropriate communication methods.
“Overall, the main challenge is ensuring a match between jobseekers’ competencies, job requirements, employers’ readiness and the workplace adjustments needed.
“Therefore, Perkeso’s approach is to build employers’ confidence through advocacy programmes that raise awareness and create opportunities for persons with visual impairments based on their capabilities and abilities,” he said.
To ensure more effective job matching, Azirruan said Perkeso conducted profiling to identify jobseekers’ academic qualifications, skills, experience, interests, functional abilities and support requirements before matching them with suitable positions.
Perkeso also recommended workplace adjustments, conducted post-placement monitoring and provided advisory services to employers to support job retention and career development among persons with visual impairments.
In the creative industry, opportunities for persons with visual impairments to develop their talents should be made available based on their abilities and skills, rather than restricted by their physical disabilities.
National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) chief executive officer Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib said visual impairment should not be used as a reason to deny someone an opportunity before their talent had been fairly assessed.
He said opportunities could be expanded to include acting, writing, story development, directing and production, depending on individuals’ skills and the support they required.
Finas is also open to considering proposals to expand employment opportunities for persons with disabilities through the Creative Content Fund, including taking into account productions that employ persons with disabilities and the costs of providing suitable facilities.
Azmir Saifuddin said proposals to introduce quotas or additional points for productions involving talent and crew members with disabilities could also be considered through engagement sessions with the disability community, MAB, industry associations and relevant stakeholders.
“In my view, an effective mechanism must take into account the quality of participation. We need to assess whether an individual is given meaningful responsibilities, fair remuneration, the support needed to work and opportunities to build professional experience.
“Simply having their names on a cast or crew list does not reflect the level of inclusivity in a production,” he said.
He said Finas was also open to collaborating with MAB and training institutions to identify talent and provide training for persons with visual impairments according to their skills, interests and industry requirements, including scriptwriting, acting, voice-over work and audio production.
Azmir Saifuddin said Finas played a role in establishing networks and facilitating opportunities, while job placement required cooperation from employers, appropriate skills matching and continuous support to ensure that persons with disabilities secured employment, received fair remuneration and built careers in the industry.
He said Finas had also organised the Creative Workshop for Persons with Disabilities: Vocals and Basic Acting (Radio Drama) in February as part of its talent development initiatives.
“Our measure of success is when persons with disabilities are given opportunities to work, receive fair remuneration and build careers in the industry,” he said.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Film Directors’ Association (FDAM) chairman Datuk Afdlin Shauki said writing and acting offered opportunities for persons with visual impairments to showcase their talents, while directing presented its own challenges because it relied heavily on visual elements.
He said they should be given the space to demonstrate their abilities through their own work, including producing short videos using smartphones to showcase their ideas and creativity.
“Things are different now. Just start with a phone and show what you want to do. If someone with a visual impairment believes they can do it, prove it by making a simple story using a phone. They can then show it to others so that people understand what they are trying to convey,” he said.
Afdlin said talent should remain the primary consideration when selecting actors and that persons with visual impairments should not be restricted to roles that portray their disabilities alone. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Govt to study identity, age checks for Roblox and online gaming platforms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The government will examine the feasibility of expanding the implementation of electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) verification and age verification to online gaming platforms such as Roblox, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the move will take into account various aspects, including issues involving underage users as well as the possibility of the platforms being abused by extremist, radical, and terrorist groups.
“In my discussions with Roblox, for example, since last year, it has shown that they are ready to cooperate. The issue might only be in terms of user verification and user age verification.
“So we will look into the suitability of expanding aspects of eKYC and age verification to platforms like Roblox,” he told reporters after the document exchange ceremony for a RM5.2 billion financing facility for Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) here today.
He said this when commenting on a statement by former Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay regarding the issue, which also encompasses underage children.
Fahmi said the government, including through the National Security Council, conducts continuous monitoring of platforms that may be misused by these groups.
He said that action will be taken by the authorities, including the Royal Malaysia Police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), if the need arises.
“We will consider various aspects, but if prompt action needs to be taken, that will certainly be carried out by the authorities,” he said.
In another development, Fahmi said he will discuss the implementation of age restriction efforts for social media users with his counterpart during a visit to Indonesia.
He is scheduled to depart for Bali this afternoon before heading to Jakarta tomorrow to attend the World Conference on Creative Economy (WCCE) 2026 and hold a series of meetings, including with ministers responsible for communications and digital, as well as culture.
“Indonesia has its own ways, its own regulatory framework, and there are differences and similarities with Malaysia. We will discuss to look at the challenges faced in discussions with these social media platform service providers,” he said.
Fahmi added that the meeting with Indonesia's Minister of Culture will, among other things, discuss Malaysia's aspiration to bring local intellectual property (IP) for viewing by the Indonesian public.
He noted that there are Malaysian works broadcast through streaming platforms like Viu that are also watched by communities in the neighbouring country.
Accordingly, he said both sides will examine ways to bridge the ties between Malaysia's and Indonesia's cinema networks, besides discussing productions that broadcast online content.
“We will also discuss, God willing, collaborative efforts between production companies, films, and creative content,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Japan explore defence technology transfer, local industry cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Malaysia and Japan have the potential to expand defence industry cooperation through technology transfer, local component development and participation in global supply chains, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
The matter was discussed during a meeting with Japan’s Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency (ATLA), led by its Commissioner Manabu Imakyurei, he added.
“I received a briefing on Japan’s approach to developing its defence industry, while exchanging views on potential cooperation in technology transfer, local component development and global supply chains.
“I believe closer ties based on trust and mutual respect will open up more opportunities for defence cooperation that benefit both countries,” he posted on X, explaining that ATLA was an agency under Japan’s Ministry of Defence responsible for defence procurement, technology and logistics.
He began a four-day official working visit to Japan yesterday, aimed at expanding defence cooperation and strengthening mutual understanding in addressing regional security challenges.
The visit, which is grounded in the Malaysia-Japan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, is also expected to further strengthen relations between the two countries. — Bernama

Title: Johor police arrest 13 over Molotov cocktail attack on Myanmar refugee homes in Kulai
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 19 — Police have detained 13 local men following a Molotov cocktail attack targeting several homes at a Myanmar refugee settlement in Kulai Besar, Kulai on October 13.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police nabbed the suspects, aged between 16 and 31, in Kulai district in an operation conducted from October 14 until yesterday.
He said the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) Criminal Investigation Department (CID), together with the Kulai District Police Headquarters (IPD) CID, carried out the arrests based on public information.
He added that checks revealed four of the suspects had a total of 12 previous criminal records related to crime and drug offences.
“Police also seized 13 mobile phones, three sets of clothing, and three baseball caps for further action,” he said in a statement today.
Ab Rahaman said police remanded four suspects for eight days beginning October 14, four for a week, and one for five days beginning October 15, while remanding four others for a week starting today.
Police are investigating the case under Section 436, Section 505(b), and Section 505(c) of the Penal Code, as well as Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 debate: Calls for fairer MP allocations, faster migrant deportations and tax relief for caregivers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The mechanism for allocating parliamentary constituency funds and the influx of foreign nationals were among the issues raised during the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill today.
Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) urged the government to enact legislation to ensure constituency allocations for MPs were distributed according to a proportional formula based on the number of voters and residents, regardless of political affiliation.
“For example, Bangi has more than 300,000 voters, the highest number in Malaysia, and a population of 700,000. Other constituencies, meanwhile, have only half or a third of Bangi’s number of voters.
“If Bangi receives the same allocation as other constituencies with far fewer voters, it would create an injustice, as voters in Bangi would have to accept, based on a rough calculation, an allocation per voter that is lower than in other areas,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dr Halimah Ali (PN-Kapar) urged the government to issue a circular directing that all MPs, including those from the Opposition bloc, be invited to attend District Action Council meetings, enabling them to monitor project implementation and raise public concerns directly.
She said the involvement of elected representatives in the meetings was important to ensure that issues affecting their respective constituencies could be brought directly to the relevant departments and agencies for more effective follow-up action.
“We want to know the progress of projects, whether they are delayed, facing problems or cancelled, and who has been awarded the projects. For example, when flash floods cause difficulties for the people, we can deal directly with the relevant departments and agencies, chaired by the district officer, so that further action can be taken,” she said.
Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) urged the government to tighten national border security controls and conduct integrated operations to comprehensively curb the entry of undocumented migrants. He said these efforts should be supported by adequate infrastructure, equipment and manpower to prevent continued incursions through illegal crossing points.
“Once the national borders have been firmly sealed, we should then clear every corner of the country of undocumented migrants,” he said, while proposing stricter requirements for hiring foreign workers and faster repatriation procedures for undocumented migrants held at immigration detention depots.
On the issue of Myanmar refugees, Radzi urged the government to clarify the registration mechanism administered by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and increase diplomatic pressure to ensure the group was resettled in third countries as soon as possible.
Also drawing attention was Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar), who proposed that the government consider income tax exemption incentives for individuals who employ domestic helpers specifically to care for their elderly parents at home.
Interjecting during the debate speech by Datuk Wan Saifulruddin Wan Jan (PN-Tasek Gelugor), he said the measure was important as Malaysia prepared to enter an ageing society phase, given that many people, particularly Malays, preferred to care for their parents at home rather than place them in care centres.
“Many people want to care for their parents at home and provide personal care. However, they are not given tax exemptions if they hire domestic helpers specifically to assist in caring for their parents,” he said.
Supporting the proposal, Wan Saiful said such an initiative could ease the financial burden on middle-income families who chose to hire domestic helpers to care for their parents at home, as the cost of private care centres could now reach RM8,000 a month.
He also urged the Health Ministry, the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry, Economy Ministry and the Finance Ministry to conduct a financing-mapping study to coordinate welfare funding for senior citizens in a holistic manner.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan police arrest man over alleged indecent act involving cat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — A man has been arrested in Kelantan to assist investigations into a viral video allegedly showing him committing an indecent act involving a cat at his home.
Pasir Puteh district police chief Superintendent Saari Yaacob said police received a report on October 18 after the video circulated on social media platform Threads.
He said police subsequently arrested a man to assist with further investigations, with the case being investigated under Section 377 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
In a statement issued today, Saari said police were treating the matter seriously and conducting a thorough investigation to establish the facts and complete their probe in accordance with the law.
He urged the public not to speculate, spread allegations or share unverified information that could jeopardise the investigation.
The public was also advised against recirculating the video out of respect for public sensitivities and to prevent the spread of inappropriate content.

Title: ‘Justice has prevailed’: Teresa Kok wins RM250,000 defamation suit against Dr Akmal over halal certification row
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Seputeh MP Teresa Kok has won RM250,000 in damages in her defamation suit against Umno Youth chief  Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh over remarks he made during a dispute on halal certification.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that the High Court in Melaka also ordered Dr Akmal to pay RM50,000 in legal costs, remove the defamatory statements from his social media accounts within seven days and refrain from repeating them or making similar remarks about Kok.
In a statement posted on Facebook, Kok said she hoped the judgment would serve as a reminder that democratic freedoms must be exercised responsibly.
“I hope this judgment serves as a reminder that democratic freedoms must be exercised responsibly. I remain steadfast in my commitment to serving the people and defending democratic values,” she said.
“The law has spoken, and justice has prevailed,” she added.
Kok said the lawsuit was not about financial gain or silencing political opponents, but about defending her dignity and upholding the rule of law.
The dispute began in September 2024 after Kok questioned a proposal to make halal certification compulsory for restaurants and food businesses that did not serve pork or alcohol, warning that the requirement could burden operators, particularly smaller businesses.
Dr Akmal responded by calling Kok an “old nyonya” and suggesting that a “non-halal” label be placed on her forehead.
Kok said political differences should be addressed through facts and reasoned debate rather than personal vilification, adding that no one should be above the law regardless of political prominence.
FMT quoted Dr Akmal’s lawyer Syahrul Syazwan Salehin as saying he would advise his client and obtain instructions before deciding whether to take further action.

Title: Selangor Sultan launches Silver Jubilee book, stamps and coins marking 25 years on throne
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah today launched a commemorative book, first-day cover and stamps, and special coins in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign.
Also present at the ceremony at Pustaka Raja Tun Uda here were Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin and Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah.
Accompanied by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, Sultan Sharafuddin officiated at the launch of the commemorative items, presented as tokens of appreciation by the Selangor government in collaboration with the Selangor State Treasury, Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) and Pos Malaysia Bhd.
In his address, Amirudin expressed appreciation to UPM for its cooperation and commitment in producing the book, titled
Menjulang Takhta: 25 Tahun Pemerintahan Sultan Selangor
.
He said the publication was a meaningful effort to document the Sultan’s reign and preserve the heritage and identity of the Selangor Sultanate for future generations.
“Today, we are also presented with special commemorative stamps produced by Pos Malaysia to showcase Selangor’s royal heritage and grandeur.
“The stamps feature images of the Balairung Seri (Throne Room) at Istana Alam Shah, the Tengkolok Balung Raja royal headdress and the Keris Terapang Gabus, alongside geometric patterns and nine-petalled Bunga Tanjung motifs symbolising the majesty of the royal institution, the sanctity of tradition and the state’s sovereignty,” he said.
Amirudin said the State Treasury had also produced special commemorative coins to mark Sultan Sharafuddin’s 25-year reign, symbolising the state’s progress, stability and prosperity.
He said the commemorative items demonstrated that the Silver Jubilee celebrations went beyond documenting history by highlighting art, symbolism and heritage of significant historical and cultural value.
“These are tokens of appreciation from the Selangor government, made possible through the cooperation and support of the State Treasury, UPM and Pos Malaysia.
“May these gifts serve as meaningful mementoes and reflect the close cooperation among the agencies for mutual benefit,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Proposed Kuching international airport could contribute RM1.8b annually to Sarawak GDP by 2050, says state minister
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 19 — The proposed New Kuching International Airport (NKIA) at Tanjung Embang could contribute approximately RM1.8 billion annually to Sarawak’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2050 under a high-growth scenario.
Sarawak Minister for Transport Datuk Seri Lee Kim Shin said the projection was among the findings of a feasibility study conducted by Netherlands Airport Consultants (NACO).
“The study also projected that NKIA could support approximately 37,919 full-time equivalent jobs across the wider economy. During construction, Phase One could support around 9,393 jobs annually over the projected six-year construction period.
“NKIA has the potential to create wider economic opportunities in tourism, aviation services and supporting industries, including air cargo, aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), aircraft parts manufacturing, as well as aerotropolis development,” he said.
Lee said this when winding up the debate for his ministry at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting here, today.
He said the completed study has concluded that Tanjung Embang is technically and operationally feasible for the proposed airport development.
“The study also projects that increased passenger traffic could generate RM3.99 billion in tourism receipts by 2050. These benefits could attract new investments, strengthen local businesses, create employment opportunities and stimulate economic growth across Sarawak,” he added. — Bernama

Title: AGC to appeal against Session Court’s decision to acquit and discharge Papagomo of sedition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will file a notice of appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision to acquit and discharge blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, of a sedition charge.
In a statement today, the AGC said the decision was made after examining the ruling of the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court sitting in the Klang Sessions Court today, which acquitted and discharged Wan Muhammad Azri, 43, at the close of the defence case for a charge under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948 (Act 15).
“After examining the decision of the Sessions Court Judge, this department has decided to file a notice of appeal against the acquittal and discharge in the near future,” the AGC said in a statement today.
According to the AGC, the prosecution had previously appealed against a decision by the same court on September 3, 2025, which had acquitted and discharged the accused at the close of the prosecution’s case.
The AGC stated that the appeal against that decision was filed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on September 4, 2025, before the court allowed the public prosecutor’s appeal on July 31 last year and ordered the accused to enter his defence after finding that the prosecution had successfully proven a prima facie case.
“The accused presented his defence by giving sworn testimony in the same Sessions Court. The accused, who was the sole defence witness, admitted to issuing seditious statements as charged and merely presented a defence in the form of a denial,” the AGC said in the statement.
Earlier, Judge Siti Aminah Ghazali acquitted and discharged Wan Muhammad Azri after finding that the defence had successfully raised reasonable doubt at the close of the defence case.
On January 8, 2024, the man pleaded not guilty to a charge of uttering seditious remarks linking the government to being pro-Israel and pro-West via Facebook.
He was allegedly accused of making the statement on the Facebook page of Halid Hamidi (Halid Mat Kool), which was later viewed by an individual at a condominium unit in Jalan Tong Shin, Bukit Bintang here at 1pm on November 8, 2023.
The charge was framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948, which carries a maximum penalty of three years in imprisonment or a fine of RM5,000, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Semporna’s illegal foreign business activities raised in Cabinet, says minister
Article:
SEMPORNA, Oct 19 — The issue of foreigners abusing social visit passes to engage in illegal economic activities in Semporna has been raised and discussed in the Federal Cabinet, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
He said the federal government takes the situation seriously and is actively carrying out enforcement action through integrated operations, particularly on popular tourist islands in the waters off the district.
“Action is being taken on this issue, with operations conducted particularly against business activities on the islands.
“The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) has also discussed this issue and will take appropriate action,” he told reporters after an official working visit today to assess border control preparedness at Pulau Ligitan, Pulau Sipadan and Pulau Mabul.
He was commenting on a special report series by the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) published in August, which highlighted how foreign investors were illegally gaining control of the district’s tourism economic chain, posing a serious threat to the security and livelihoods of the local population.
According to the reports, the Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) also exposed how foreigners used illegal partnerships or local proxies in “Ali Baba” arrangements to control services, resorts, and tourism facilities, creating opportunities for various criminal activities, including operating scam centres.
Commenting on the same reports, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had directed ESSCom to conduct joint enforcement operations with all relevant parties in the area, including local authorities. — Bernama

Title: Sabah registers 38,659 commercial vehicles under subsidised diesel scheme
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 19 — A total of 38,659 commercial vehicles belonging to 17,703 companies in Sabah have registered under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) as of yesterday, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali
He said the registrations comprised 27,655 vehicles transporting essential goods, 8,773 company-owned vehicles, including jeeps and pick-up trucks, and 2,231 public land transport vehicles.
“Nationwide, 514,111 commercial vehicles belonging to 205,167 companies had registered under SKDS as of October 18,” he said in a statement after visiting Pulau Banggi in Kudat today.
Armizan said 1,408 vehicles belonging to 995 companies in Sabah had also registered under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS).
These comprised 788 public land transport vehicles and 620 vehicles transporting essential goods. Separately, one registration was recorded for the water public transport sector in Sabah.
At the national level, 44,883 vehicles belonging to 24,204 companies had registered under SKPS.
Armizan said the ministry (KPDN) oversees fuel subsidy distribution to eligible commercial vehicles through SKDS and SKPS to ensure assistance is channelled to the intended sectors.
The schemes cover public land transport, vehicles transporting essential goods and eligible privately owned business vehicles operated by micro and small enterprises. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak targets 15,000MW power capacity by 2035, with 60pc from renewables
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 19 — Sarawak aims for an electricity generation capacity of 15,000 megawatts (MW) by 2035, with at least 60 per cent coming from renewable energy sources.
Sarawak Minister of Utility and Telecommunication Datuk Seri Julaihi Narawi said that to achieve this target, three major projects with a total capacity of 3,285 MW are currently being implemented: the Baleh hydroelectric project, the Samalaju Combined Cycle Power Plant (CCPP), and the Miri Combined Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT).
“The Baleh hydroelectric plant, with a capacity of 1,285 MW, is expected to operate in the fourth quarter of 2029. The Samalaju CCPP, with a capacity of 1,500 MW, is scheduled to operate in phases, with Blocks 1 and 2 having a total capacity of 1,000 MW expected to operate in the second quarter of 2027, while Block 3 with a capacity of 500 MW is scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.
“The Miri CCGT, with a capacity of 500 MW, has now achieved 63 percent physical progress and is expected to start operating in the fourth quarter of 2027,” he said.
Julaihi said this when winding up the debate for his ministry at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting here, today.
Meanwhile, Julaihi said Sarawak continues to strengthen its role as the Battery of Asean through the development of the Borneo Power Grid and the Asean Power Grid.
“Currently, Sarawak exports an average of 100 MW to West Kalimantan and 30 MW to Sabah. The government is also planning electricity exports to Brunei of at least 30 MW, Singapore of not exceeding 1,000 MW, and Peninsular Malaysia of not less than 1,000 MW.
“The interconnection project to Brunei is still in negotiations and feasibility studies, Singapore is in the submarine cable survey study stage, while Peninsular Malaysia is in early discussions,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia retains WHO validation for eliminating mother-to-child HIV, syphilis transmission
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Malaysia has retained the World Health Organisation (WHO) validation for the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis following an assessment of the country’s achievements from 2021 to 2024.
In a statement, the Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement reaffirmed the recognition first obtained in 2018, when Malaysia became the first country in the WHO Western Pacific Region to receive the validation.
The ministry said the recognition reflected Malaysia’s continued commitment to strengthening maternal and child health and ensuring access to quality screening, treatment and healthcare services.
It added that the achievement demonstrated the effectiveness of the Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission (PMTCT) of HIV and Syphilis programme, which has been integrated into the country’s maternal and child health services since 1997.
The certificate and recognition were received by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad at the 77th WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific meeting in Manila today.
According to the MOH, screening coverage for HIV and syphilis among pregnant women remained above 95 per cent throughout the assessment period, while antiretroviral treatment coverage among pregnant women living with HIV reached approximately 99 per cent.
In 2024, the mother-to-child HIV transmission rate stood at 1.52 per cent, meeting the WHO target of below two per cent.
The ministry also reported that the rate of congenital syphilis, an infection transmitted from mother to child during pregnancy, stood at 10 cases per 100,000 live births, well below the WHO elimination threshold of 50 cases per 100,000 live births.
The MOH attributed the achievement to the sustained commitment of healthcare personnel at all levels and collaboration among government agencies, private healthcare providers, the Malaysian AIDS Council, civil society organisations and the community.
The ministry also expressed appreciation to all parties involved, as well as the WHO, for its technical support and cooperation.
It said efforts would continue to strengthen early detection, treatment and follow-up care for mothers and infants to sustain the achievement.
The MOH also advised pregnant women to seek antenatal care as early as possible and complete the recommended screening and treatment procedures to protect their health and that of their babies. — Bernama

Title: Data Centre Bill to go to Cabinet in 2027, says Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — The government plans to draft the Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill for submission to the Cabinet next year to regulate the growth of the data centre industry in line with the country’s energy and water supply capacity.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the measure aims to ensure that investments in the industry add value to the domestic economy, in addition to addressing utility constraints and avoiding imbalances in environmental impact.
He said the proposal to draft the bill is part of the strategic regulatory plan agreed upon by the National Economic Action Council (NEAC) at a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today.
He said the agreement was reached following the presentation of the National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development by the Ministry of Digital.
“This step is taken to address utility constraints, avoid environmental impact imbalances, and ensure that data centre investments provide real economic spillovers to the local digital ecosystem,” he said in a statement.
Akmal Nasrullah said NEAC also agreed that the four lead ministries, along with the implementing agencies, would adopt the Circular Economy Framework (CEF) presented by the Ministry of Economy.
“NEAC agreed that the lead ministries, namely the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, and the Ministry of Human Resources, along with the implementing agencies, should adopt the CEF with an integrated governance, monitoring, and coordination structure,” he said.
He noted that the framework aims to lead the country’s transition from a linear economic model based on the “use-and-dispose” concept to a circular economy that optimises the lifespan of materials, reduces waste and preserves the value of resources.
“This integrated policy was formulated to address the issue of fragmented implementation across ministries in the past, to avoid economic losses due to the loss of valuable resources, and to support the Net Zero aspiration by 2050,” he said.
In other developments, Akmal Nasrullah said the meeting also reviewed the National Economic Resilience Framework presented by the Economic Affairs Division, Prime Minister’s Office, as a comprehensive long-term measure to address external economic shocks.
“The meeting agreed that this proposal should be presented to the Cabinet and further discussed at a meeting of ministry secretaries-general and heads of service chaired by the Chief Secretary to the Government,” he said.
He highlighted that NEAC today examined three strategic policy priorities to drive sustainable growth and strengthen the resilience of the country’s economy in the face of structural challenges and global economic uncertainties.
He said the agreed policies must be implemented in an integrated manner, particularly to enhance the efficiency of resource use, ensure that data centre investments add value to the domestic economy, and strengthen the country’s preparedness to face external economic shocks.
Akmal Nasrullah said the Ministry of Economy, as the NEAC secretariat, will coordinate and monitor follow-up actions with the relevant ministries and implementing agencies.
“The government’s priority is not just growth and investment, but a more productive, sustainable, and resilient economy with real benefits for the people and businesses,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Rapid KL to deploy 85 shuttle buses for Malaysian GP at Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct19 — Rapid KL will deploy 85 buses for a special shuttle service to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) in conjunction with the 2026 Petronas Grand Prix (GP) of Malaysia from October 30 to November 1.
Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the service was aimed at meeting the transport needs of motorsports fans and facilitating their journeys to the circuit.
He said tickets would go on sale from October 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni Bus Hub.
“Every year, motorsports fans from various locations gather in Sepang to experience the excitement of this world-class race firsthand. Rapid KL hopes this service will make their journeys to the circuit easier and more comfortable,” he said in a statement today.
Syahrul Azmir said the shuttle service would operate from three main locations, namely the Pasar Seni Bus Hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 Bus Hub.
A one-way ticket from Pasar Seni or the KLCC bus stop will cost RM20, while a return ticket will be priced at RM35. The one-way fare from KLIA Terminal 2 is RM12.
Buses travelling to SIC from all three locations will operate from 7 am to 1 pm at 30-minute intervals, while return services from the circuit will run from 4 pm to 7 pm.
In collaboration with SIC, Rapid KL will also provide a free shuttle service around the circuit throughout the event to facilitate visitors’ movement.
The public is advised to purchase tickets in advance to avoid long queues and waiting times. Further information is available on the official MyRapid website and through the MyRapid PULSE app. — Bernama
